title.zh: 卷三百六十五 列傳第一百二十四 岳飛
title.raw: 卷三百六十五 列傳第一百二十四 岳飛 Volume 365 Biographies 124: Yue Fei

sentences.zh: 岳飛子:雲

translations.literal: Yue Fei's son: Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei's son: Yun.

sentences.zh: 岳飛字鵬舉，相州湯陰人。

translations.literal: Yue Fei, styled Pengju, was a man of Tangyin in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei, whose courtesy name was Pengju, came from Tangyin in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 世力農。

translations.literal: For generations the family were vigorous farmers.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed the land with their own hands for generations.

sentences.zh: 父和，能節食以濟饑者。

translations.literal: His father He was able to stint his own food to relieve the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue He was known for going without meals himself so that he could feed those who were starving.

sentences.zh: 有耕侵其地，割而與之；

translations.literal: When a neighbor's plowing encroached on his land, he cut off the disputed strip and gave it to the neighbor;
translations.idiomatic: If a neighbor's plowing crossed into his fields, he would cede the disputed strip rather than quarrel;

sentences.zh: 貰其財者不責償。

translations.literal: those who borrowed goods from him he did not demand repayment.
translations.idiomatic: and he never pressed those who borrowed from him to repay.

sentences.zh: 飛生時，有大禽若鵠，飛鳴室上，因以為名。

translations.literal: When Fei was born, a great bird like a swan flew crying above the house, and on this account he was given his name.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth a great bird resembling a swan flew circling and crying over the house, and from this omen he received the name Fei.

sentences.zh: 未彌月，河決內黃，水暴至，母姚抱飛坐甕中，衝濤及岸得免，人 少負氣節，沈厚寡言，家貧力學，尤好《左氏春秋》、孫吳兵法。

translations.literal: Before he was a full month old the Yellow River burst at Neihuang, floodwaters rushed in, his mother Yao held Fei seated in a jar, borne by the current to the bank where they escaped; people marveled at this. From youth he possessed integrity and spirit, was deep and taciturn, studied diligently though poor, and especially loved the Zuo Commentary and the military writings of Sun and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was even a month old the Yellow River broke through at Neihuang and a sudden flood swept in; his mother Yao clutched the infant Fei inside a large jar, and the torrent carried them to shore where both survived—a marvel to all who heard of it. Even as a boy he showed fierce integrity, a grave and quiet manner, and an appetite for learning despite poverty; above all he cherished the Zuo Commentary and the Art of War attributed to Sun and Wu.

sentences.zh: 生有神力，未冠，挽弓三百斤，弩八石。

translations.literal: He was born with divine strength; before coming of age he could draw a bow of three hundred jin and a crossbow of eight shi.
translations.idiomatic: Nature had endowed him with extraordinary strength: before he came of age he could draw a three-hundred-jin bow and an eight-stone crossbow.

sentences.zh: 學射於周同，盡其術，能左右射。

translations.literal: He studied archery under Zhou Tong, mastered all his techniques, and could shoot with either hand.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in archery under Zhou Tong, mastered every technique his teacher knew, and could shoot equally well with either hand.

sentences.zh: 同死，朔望設祭於其冢。

translations.literal: When Tong died, on the first and fifteenth of each month he set out offerings at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong's death he made offerings at his teacher's grave on the first and fifteenth of every month.

sentences.zh: 父義之，曰：「汝為時用，其徇國死義乎。」

translations.literal: His father approved of this and said, "When you are employed by the age, will you not die for the state and righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: His father was moved by this devotion and said, "When your hour comes to serve the realm, will you not give your life for country and principle?"

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，真定宣撫劉韐募敢戰士，飛應募。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuanhe, Liu Yan, Pacification Commissioner of Zhending, recruited bold fighters; Fei answered the call.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Xuanhe reign, Liu Yan, the Pacification Commissioner at Zhending, raised a corps of daring fighters, and Yue Fei enlisted.

sentences.zh: 相有劇賊陶俊、賈進和，飛請百騎滅之。

translations.literal: In Xiang there were fierce bandits Tao Jun and Jia Jinhe; Fei asked for a hundred horsemen to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangzhou two notorious bandit chiefs, Tao Jun and Jia Jinhe, were ravaging the countryside; Yue Fei volunteered a hundred horsemen to wipe them out.

sentences.zh: 遣卒偽為商入賊境，賊掠以充部伍。

translations.literal: He sent soldiers disguised as merchants into the bandits' territory; the bandits seized them to swell their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men disguised as merchants into bandit country; the raiders seized them to reinforce their own ranks.

sentences.zh: 飛遣百人伏山下，自領數十騎逼賊壘。

translations.literal: Fei posted a hundred men in ambush below the hill and himself led several dozen horsemen to press the bandit stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei hid a hundred men below the hill while he personally led several dozen horsemen to provoke the bandit camp.

sentences.zh: 賊出戰，飛陽北，賊來追之，伏兵起，先所遣卒擒俊及進和以歸。

translations.literal: The bandits came out to fight; Fei feigned flight northward, and when they pursued, the ambush rose; the soldiers earlier sent in disguise seized Jun and Jinhe and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits sallied forth; Yue Fei pretended to flee north, drawing them in pursuit until the ambush struck. The disguised men inside their ranks seized Tao Jun and Jia Jinhe and brought them in.

sentences.zh: 康王至相，飛因劉浩見，命招賊吉倩，倩以衆三百八十人降。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang came to Xiang, Fei was introduced through Liu Hao; he was ordered to summon the bandit Ji Qian, and Qian surrendered with a force of three hundred eighty men.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang arrived at Xiangzhou, Yue Fei was presented through Liu Hao and ordered to win over the bandit Ji Qian, who surrendered with three hundred and eighty followers.

sentences.zh: 補承信郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supplementary Gentleman for Trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as Gentleman for Trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 以鐵騎三百往李固渡嘗敵，敗之。

translations.literal: With three hundred armored horsemen he went to Ligudu to probe the enemy and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Leading three hundred armored horsemen to Ligudu, he tested the enemy in battle and put them to rout.

sentences.zh: 從浩解東京圍，與敵相持於滑南，領百騎習兵河上。

translations.literal: Following Hao in relieving the siege of the Eastern Capital, he faced the enemy south of Hua and led a hundred horsemen to drill troops along the river.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Hao in lifting the siege of the Eastern Capital and, while the armies faced each other south of Hua, led a hundred horsemen in riverbank drills.

sentences.zh: 敵猝至，飛麾其徒曰：「敵雖衆，未知吾虛實，當及其未定擊之。

translations.literal: The enemy came suddenly; Fei waved his men on and said, "Though the foe are many, they do not yet know our strength; we should strike while they are unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy appeared without warning. Yue Fei rallied his men: "They are numerous but do not yet know our strength—strike before they can steady themselves."

sentences.zh: 」乃獨馳迎敵。

translations.literal: " He then charged alone to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he galloped alone toward the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 有梟將舞刀而前，飛斬之，敵大敗。

translations.literal: A fierce general flourished his blade and came forward; Fei cut him down, and the enemy were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce enemy officer came whirling his blade; Yue Fei struck him down at a stroke, and the foe collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 遷秉義郎，隸留守宗澤。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman Upholding Righteousness and placed under the garrison commander Zong Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Gentleman Upholding Righteousness, he entered the service of the garrison commander Zong Ze.

sentences.zh: 戰開德、曹州皆有功，澤大奇之，曰：「爾勇智才藝，古良將不能過，然好野戰，非萬全計。

translations.literal: In battles at Kaide and Caozhou he distinguished himself; Ze marveled greatly at him and said, "Your courage, wisdom, talent, and skill surpass the great generals of old, yet you favor wild fighting—it is not a plan of perfect safety."
translations.idiomatic: He won credit fighting at Kaide and Caozhou. Zong Ze was deeply impressed and told him, "In courage, wit, and martial skill you outshine the great captains of antiquity—yet your taste for open battle is not the surest path to victory."

sentences.zh: 」因授以陣圖。

translations.literal: " He thereupon taught him battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: " He then instructed him in formal battle arrays.

sentences.zh: 飛曰：「陣而後戰，兵法之常，運用之妙，存乎一心。

translations.literal: Fei said, "To array the troops before fighting is the constant rule of war; the subtlety of application lies in the mind alone."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei replied, "Deploying formations before battle is the constant teaching of the art of war—but the subtlety of how they are used rests entirely in the commander's mind."

sentences.zh: 」澤是其言。

translations.literal: " Ze approved of his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Zong Ze agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 康王即位，飛上書數千言，大略謂：「陛下已登大寶，社稷有主，已足伐敵之謀，而勤王之師日集，彼方謂吾素弱，宜乘其怠擊之。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang took the throne, Fei submitted a memorial of several thousand characters, in substance saying: "Your Majesty has ascended the great throne; the altars of state have a lord—enough to thwart the enemy's designs. Armies rallying to the throne gather daily; they still think us chronically weak. We should strike while they are slack."
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Kang ascended the throne, Yue Fei submitted a memorial thousands of characters long. Its gist was: "Your Majesty now holds the Mandate; the realm again has a sovereign, enough in itself to unsettle the enemy's plans. Armies loyal to the throne gather by the day, yet the Jurchens still take us for the weak state we were—this is the moment to strike while their guard is down."

sentences.zh: 黃潛善、汪伯彥輩不能承聖意恢復，奉車駕日益南，恐不足繫中原之望。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan, Wang Boyan, and their like cannot carry out the sacred intent of recovery; they escort the imperial carriage ever farther south—I fear this will not satisfy the hopes of the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan fail to carry out Your Majesty's will to recover the north, driving the court ever deeper into the south. I fear the heartland will lose faith in us.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下乘敵穴未固，親率六軍北渡，則將士作氣，中原可復。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty, while the enemy's foothold is not yet firm, to lead the Six Armies north across the river; then officers and soldiers will take heart, and the Central Plains can be recovered."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty, while the enemy's grip is not yet secure, to lead the imperial armies north across the river yourself. The troops will take fresh heart, and the Central Plains can be won back."

sentences.zh: 」書聞，以越職奪官歸。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was received, he was stripped of office for overstepping his post and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, he was dismissed for overstepping his authority and sent home.

sentences.zh: 詣河北招討使張所，所待以國士，借補修武郎，充中軍統領。

translations.literal: He went to Zhang Suo, Pacification Commissioner of Hebei; Suo treated him as a man of the highest caliber, provisionally appointed him Gentleman of Cultivated Martiality, and made him commander of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself to Zhang Suo, the Hebei Pacification Commissioner, who received him as a peerless talent, gave him provisional rank as Gentleman of Cultivated Martiality, and made him commander of the central army.

sentences.zh: 所問曰：「汝能敵幾何？

translations.literal: Suo asked him, "How many can you match in battle?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suo asked him, "How many foes can you take on?"

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「勇不足恃，用兵在先定謀，欒枝曳柴以敗荊，莫敖采樵以致絞，皆謀定也。

translations.literal: " Fei said, "Courage alone cannot be relied on; in employing troops the first thing is to fix the plan. Luan Zhi dragged brushwood to defeat Chu; the Mo'ao gathered firewood to bring down Jiao—all were settled by strategy."
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei answered, "Bravery alone is not enough. War is won by planning first. Luan Zhi dragged brushwood to defeat Chu; the Mo'ao gathered firewood to destroy Jiao—victory came from strategy, not sheer daring."

sentences.zh: 」所矍然曰：「君殆非行伍中人。

translations.literal: " Suo started in alarm and said, "Sir, you are scarcely a man of the ranks."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Suo started in surprise. "You are scarcely a common soldier," he said.

sentences.zh: 」飛因說之曰：「國家都汴，恃河北以為固。

translations.literal: " Fei then urged him, saying, "The state has its capital at Bian; it relies on Hebei for security."
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei went on: "The dynasty holds its capital at Bianjing and depends on Hebei for its security."

sentences.zh: 苟馮據要衝，峙列重鎮，一城受圍，則諸城或撓或救，金人不能窺河南，而京師根本之地固矣。

translations.literal: If we hold the strategic passes and set up strong garrisons in array, when one city is besieged the others will harass or relieve it; the Jin will not be able to peer into the lands south of the Yellow River, and the capital's root territory will be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the vital crossings, plant strong garrisons in depth—if one city is besieged, the others can harass or relieve it. The Jin will not dare probe south of the river, and the capital's foundations will stand firm."

sentences.zh: 招撫誠能提兵壓境，飛唯命是從。

translations.literal: If the Commissioner truly can lead troops to press the border, Fei will obey your every command."
translations.idiomatic: If you, Commissioner, will truly lead troops to the frontier, I am yours to command."

sentences.zh: 」所大喜，借補武經郎。

translations.literal: " Suo was greatly pleased and provisionally appointed him Gentleman of Martial Classics.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Suo was delighted and gave him provisional rank as Gentleman of Martial Classics.

sentences.zh: 命從王彥渡河，至新鄉，金兵盛，彥不敢進。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow Wang Yan in crossing the river; reaching Xinxiang, the Jin forces were strong and Yan dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to cross the river under Wang Yan, he reached Xinxiang to find the Jin in overwhelming strength; Yan would not advance.

sentences.zh: 飛獨引所部鏖戰，奪其纛而舞，諸軍爭奮，遂拔新鄉。

translations.literal: Fei alone led his command in fierce fighting, seized the enemy standard and flourished it, and all the armies strove to outdo one another and took Xinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei alone led his men into bitter fighting, snatched the enemy standard and whirled it overhead, and the whole army surged forward until Xinxiang fell.

sentences.zh: 翌日，戰侯兆川，身被十餘創，士皆死戰，又敗之。

translations.literal: The next day they fought at Houzhao River; he received more than ten wounds, his soldiers all fought to the death, and again they defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The next day at Houzhao River he took more than ten wounds while his men fought as if death meant nothing, and again routed the foe.

sentences.zh: 夜屯石門山下，或傳金兵復至，一軍皆驚，飛堅臥不動，金兵卒不來。

translations.literal: At night they encamped below Shimen Mountain; a rumor spread that Jin troops had returned, and the whole army was alarmed, but Fei lay firm and unmoving, and in the end the Jin did not come.
translations.idiomatic: That night they camped below Shimen Mountain. Rumors that the Jin were returning threw the army into panic, but Yue Fei lay unmoved in his tent—and no enemy came.

sentences.zh: 食盡，走彥壁乞糧，彥不許。

translations.literal: When provisions were exhausted he went to Yan's camp to beg grain; Yan would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies ran out he went to Yan's camp to beg grain; Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 飛引兵益北，戰于太行山，擒金將拓跋耶烏。

translations.literal: Fei led his troops farther north, fought on the Taihang Mountains, and captured the Jin general Tuo-ba Ye-wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei pushed farther north, fought on the Taihang range, and captured the Jin general Tuo-ba Yewu.

sentences.zh: 居數日，復遇敵，飛單騎持丈八鐵槍，刺殺黑風大王，敵衆敗走。

translations.literal: After several days they met the enemy again; Fei alone on horseback wielded an eighteen-foot iron spear, stabbed and killed the Black Wind King, and the enemy masses fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Days later they met the enemy again. Yue Fei charged alone with an eighteen-foot iron spear, killed the Black Wind King, and put the whole host to flight.

sentences.zh: 飛自知與彥有隙，復歸宗澤，為留守司統制。

translations.literal: Knowing he was at odds with Yan, Fei returned to Zong Ze and served as controller of the garrison headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Aware that he and Yan were at odds, he returned to Zong Ze and was made controller of the garrison headquarters.

sentences.zh: 澤卒，杜充代之，飛居故職。

translations.literal: When Ze died, Du Chong replaced him, and Fei remained in his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Ze died, Du Chong succeeded him, and Yue Fei kept his former post.

sentences.zh: 二年，戰胙城，又戰黑龍潭，皆大捷。

translations.literal: In the second year he fought at Zuocheng and again at Black Dragon Pool, winning great victories in both.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he fought at Zuocheng and again at Black Dragon Pool, winning resounding victories in both.

sentences.zh: 從閭勍保護陵寢，大戰汜水關，射殪金將，大破其衆。

translations.literal: Following Lü Qin in guarding the imperial tombs, he fought a great battle at Sishui Pass, shot and killed a Jin general, and routed their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Lü Qin to guard the imperial tombs, he fought a major battle at Sishui Pass, shot a Jin general dead, and shattered their army.

sentences.zh: 駐軍竹蘆渡，與敵相持，選精銳三百伏前山下，令各以薪芻交縛兩束，夜半，爇四端而舉之。

translations.literal: He encamped at Zhulu Ford and faced the enemy in stalemate; he chose three hundred elite troops in ambush below the forward hill, ordering each to bind two bundles of brush crosswise, and at midnight to light all four ends and raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Encamped at Zhulu Ford in stalemate with the enemy, he hid three hundred picked men below the forward hill, each with two crossed bundles of brushwood; at midnight they lit all four ends and raised them high.

sentences.zh: 金人疑援兵至，驚潰。

translations.literal: The Jin suspected reinforcements had arrived and fled in alarm and rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took the torches for a fresh army and broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 三年，賊王善、曹成、孔彥舟等合衆五十萬，薄南薰門。

translations.literal: In the third year the bandits Wang Shan, Cao Cheng, Kong Yanzou, and others united a force of five hundred thousand and pressed upon the Nanxun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the bandit leaders Wang Shan, Cao Cheng, and Kong Yanzou combined half a million men and pressed against the Nanxun Gate.

sentences.zh: 飛所部僅八百，衆懼不敵，飛曰：「吾為諸君破之。

translations.literal: Fei's command numbered only eight hundred; the troops feared they could not match the foe. Fei said, "I will break them for you."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei had only eight hundred men; his troops feared the odds were impossible. He told them, "I will break them for you."

sentences.zh: 」左挾弓，右運矛，橫衝其陣，賊亂，大敗之。

translations.literal: " With bow in his left hand and spear in his right he charged across their formation; the bandits fell into disorder and were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " Bow in his left hand and spear in his right, he drove straight through their lines; the bandits broke ranks and were utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 又擒賊杜叔五、孫海于東明。

translations.literal: He also captured the bandits Du Shuwu and Sun Hai at Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured the bandits Du Shuwu and Sun Hai at Dongming.

sentences.zh: 借補英州刺史。

translations.literal: He was provisionally appointed prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received provisional appointment as prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王善圍陳州，飛戰于清河，擒其將孫勝、孫清，授真刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Shan besieged Chenzhou; Fei fought at Qinghe, captured his generals Sun Sheng and Sun Qing, and was given regular appointment as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shan besieged Chenzhou, Yue Fei fought him at Qinghe, captured his generals Sun Sheng and Sun Qing, and received full appointment as prefect.

sentences.zh: 杜充將還建康，飛曰：「中原地尺寸不可棄，今一舉足，此地非我有，他日欲復取之，非數十萬衆不可。

translations.literal: When Du Chong was about to return to Jiankang, Fei said, "Not a foot of the Central Plains can be abandoned. If we move one step now, this land will no longer be ours; to recover it later will require not less than several hundred thousand troops."
translations.idiomatic: As Du Chong prepared to withdraw to Jiankang, Yue Fei protested: "We cannot yield a single foot of the Central Plains. One step back and this land is lost to us forever—to win it back will take hundreds of thousands of men."

sentences.zh: 」充不聽，遂與俱歸。

translations.literal: " Chong would not listen, and Fei withdrew with him.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Chong would not listen, and Yue Fei withdrew with him.

sentences.zh: 師次鐵路步，遇賊張用，至六合遇李成，與戰，皆敗之。

translations.literal: The army halted at Tielubu, met the bandit Zhang Yong, and at Liuhe met Li Cheng; in battle he defeated them both.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Tielubu, routed the bandit Zhang Yong, and at Liuhe met Li Cheng in battle and defeated him as well.

sentences.zh: 成遣輕騎劫憲臣犒軍銀帛，飛進兵掩擊之，成奔江西。

translations.literal: Cheng sent light cavalry to seize the silver and silks the imperial commissioner was bringing to reward the army; Fei advanced and struck them from ambush, and Cheng fled to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng sent light cavalry to seize the silver and silks meant to reward the troops; Yue Fei struck from ambush and drove Cheng into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時命充守建康，金人與成合寇烏江，充閉門不出。

translations.literal: At the time Chong was ordered to guard Jiankang; the Jin joined Cheng in raiding Wujiang, and Chong shut the gates and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong was then ordered to hold Jiankang. The Jin allied with Li Cheng to attack Wujiang, but Chong barred the gates and would not march out.

sentences.zh: 飛泣諫請視師，充竟不出。

translations.literal: Fei wept as he remonstrated and begged to inspect the army; Chong in the end did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei wept as he begged permission to take the field; Chong still would not budge.

sentences.zh: 金人遂由馬家渡渡江，充遣飛等迎戰，王𤫉先遁，諸將皆潰，獨飛力戰。

translations.literal: The Jin then crossed the Yangzi at Majia Ford; Chong sent Fei and others to meet them in battle. Wang Yuan fled first, the other generals all broke, and Fei alone fought on with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin crossed the Yangzi at Majia Ford. Du Chong sent Yue Fei and others to meet them; Wang Yuan fled first, the other generals collapsed, and only Yue Fei fought on.

sentences.zh: 會充已降金，諸將多行剽掠，惟飛軍秋毫無所犯。

translations.literal: When Chong had already surrendered to the Jin, many generals went about plundering, but Fei's army violated not the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chong had surrendered to the Jin; most generals turned to plunder, but Yue Fei's men touched not a single thing that was not theirs.

sentences.zh: 兀朮趨杭州，飛要擊至廣德境中，六戰皆捷，擒其將王權，俘簽軍首領四十餘。

translations.literal: Wuzhu pressed toward Hangzhou; Fei harassed him into the territory of Guangde, winning six battles in succession, capturing his general Wang Quan, and taking more than forty leaders of the drafted army.
translations.idiomatic: As Wuzhu pushed toward Hangzhou, Yue Fei harried him deep into Guangde territory, winning six battles in a row, capturing the general Wang Quan, and taking more than forty drafted-army chieftains prisoner.

sentences.zh: 察其可用者，結以恩遣還，令夜斫營縱火，飛乘亂縱擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Those he judged usable he bound with kindness and sent back, ordering them to cut into the camp and set fires by night; Fei struck amid the chaos and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Those he judged useful he won over and sent back, ordering them to raid the camp and set fires that night; Yue Fei charged into the confusion and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 駐軍鍾村，軍無見糧，將士忍饑，不敢擾民。

translations.literal: He encamped at Zhong Village; the army had no grain in sight, officers and soldiers endured hunger, and dared not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Zhong Village with no grain in sight; his men went hungry rather than trouble the local people.

sentences.zh: 金所籍兵相謂曰：「此岳爺爺軍。

translations.literal: The drafted soldiers in Jin service said to one another, "This is Grandfather Yue's army."
translations.idiomatic: Jin conscripts said to one another, "This is Marshal Yue's army."

sentences.zh: 」爭來降附。

translations.literal: " They vied to come over and submit.
translations.idiomatic: " They flocked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 四年，兀朮攻常州，宜興令迎飛移屯焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wuzhu attacked Changzhou; the magistrate of Yixing welcomed Fei to move his camp there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wuzhu attacked Changzhou; the magistrate of Yixing invited Yue Fei to shift his camp there.

sentences.zh: 盜郭吉聞飛來，遁入湖，飛遣王貴、傅慶追破之，又遣辯士馬皐、林聚盡降其衆。

translations.literal: The bandit Guo Ji, hearing Fei had come, fled into the lake; Fei sent Wang Gui and Fu Qing in pursuit to defeat him, and also sent the envoys Ma Gao and Lin Ju to bring all his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Guo Ji fled into the lakes when he heard Yue Fei was coming; Wang Gui and Fu Qing ran him down, and envoys Ma Gao and Lin Ju persuaded his whole following to submit.

sentences.zh: 有張威武者不從，飛單騎入其營，斬之。

translations.literal: There was one Zhang Weiwu who would not submit; Fei rode alone into his camp and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhang Weiwu refused to yield; Yue Fei rode alone into his camp and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 避地者賴以免，圖飛像祠之。

translations.literal: Those who had fled the turmoil were spared on his account and painted his image to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees owed their safety to him and painted his portrait for worship.

sentences.zh: 金人再攻常州，飛四戰皆捷；

translations.literal: The Jin again attacked Changzhou; Fei fought four battles and won them all;
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin again attacked Changzhou, Yue Fei fought four battles and won every one;

sentences.zh: 尾襲於鎮江東，又捷；

translations.literal: pursued and struck them east of Zhenjiang, again victorious;
translations.idiomatic: pursued them east of Zhenjiang and won again;

sentences.zh: 戰于清水亭，又大捷，橫屍十五里。

translations.literal: fought at Qingshui Pavilion and won another great victory, corpses strewn for fifteen li.
translations.idiomatic: and at Qingshui Pavilion won another crushing victory, with enemy dead lying thick for fifteen li.

sentences.zh: 兀朮趨建康，飛設伏牛頭山待之。

translations.literal: Wuzhu pressed toward Jiankang; Fei set an ambush on Ox Head Mountain to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu pressed toward Jiankang; Yue Fei laid an ambush on Ox Head Mountain to receive him.

sentences.zh: 夜，令百人黑衣混金營中擾之，金兵驚，自相攻擊。

translations.literal: By night he ordered a hundred men in black to mingle in the Jin camp and raise havoc; the Jin troops were alarmed and attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: By night he sent a hundred men in black to slip into the Jin camp and sow chaos; the Jin panicked and turned on one another.

sentences.zh: 兀朮次龍灣，飛以騎三百、步兵二千馳至新城，大破之。

translations.literal: Wuzhu halted at Longwan; Fei with three hundred horsemen and two thousand foot soldiers galloped to Xincheng and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu halted at Longwan; Yue Fei raced to Xincheng with three hundred horsemen and two thousand foot soldiers and shattered his force.

sentences.zh: 兀朮奔淮西，遂復建康。

translations.literal: Wuzhu fled west of the Huai, and Jiankang was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu fled west of the Huai, and Jiankang was recovered.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「建康為要害之地，宜選兵固守，仍益兵守淮，拱護腹心。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "Jiankang is a vital place; picked troops should be chosen to hold it firmly, and still more troops posted to guard the Huai, protecting the heartland like an arch."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei memorialized: "Jiankang is the key to the south. Hold it with picked troops and reinforce the Huai line to shield the court's heartland."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 兀朮歸，飛邀擊于靜安，敗之。

translations.literal: As Wuzhu withdrew, Fei intercepted him at Jing'an and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: As Wuzhu withdrew, Yue Fei intercepted him at Jing'an and put him to rout.

sentences.zh: 詔討戚方，飛以三千人營于苦嶺。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the campaign against Qi Fang; Fei encamped at Kul Ridge with three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to suppress Qi Fang, Yue Fei encamped three thousand men at Kul Ridge.

sentences.zh: 方遁，俄益兵來，飛自領兵千人，戰數十合，皆捷。

translations.literal: Fang fled, but soon reinforced troops came; Fei personally led a thousand men, fought several dozen engagements, and won them all.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fled, then returned with reinforcements; Yue Fei personally led a thousand men through dozens of clashes and won every one.

sentences.zh: 會張俊兵至，方遂降。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun's troops arrived, Fang then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun's army arrived, Fang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 范宗尹言張俊自浙西來，盛稱飛可用，遷通、泰鎮撫使兼知泰州。

translations.literal: Fan Zongyin reported that Zhang Jun, coming from western Zhe, had lavishly praised Fei's usefulness; Fei was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of Tong and Tai and concurrently prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin reported that Zhang Jun, arriving from western Zhe, had spoken highly of Yue Fei's abilities; he was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of Tong and Tai and made prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 飛辭，乞淮南東路一重難任使，收復本路州郡，乘機漸進，使山東、河北、河東、京畿等路次第而復。

translations.literal: Fei declined, begging for a single heavy commission on the Huainan East Circuit, to recover the prefectures and districts of that circuit, advance step by step as opportunity allowed, and bring back in turn the circuits of Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, the capital region, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei declined, asking instead for a demanding post on the Huainan East Circuit so he could recover its prefectures, advance as openings appeared, and win back Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, the capital region, and the rest in turn.

sentences.zh: 會金攻楚急，詔張俊援之。

translations.literal: Just then the Jin pressed Chu hotly; an edict ordered Zhang Jun to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Jin pressed Chu hard; the court ordered Zhang Jun to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 俊辭，乃遣飛行，而命劉光世出兵援飛。

translations.literal: Jun declined, and so Fei was sent instead, while Liu Guangshi was ordered to march out to support Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun declined, so Yue Fei was sent instead, with Liu Guangshi ordered to march to his support.

sentences.zh: 飛屯三墪為楚援，尋抵承州，三戰三捷，殺高太保，俘酋長七十餘人。

translations.literal: Fei encamped at Sanpu to support Chu, soon reached Chengzhou, won three battles in three victories, killed Gao the Grand Guardian, and captured more than seventy chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei encamped at Sanpu to relieve Chu, then reached Chengzhou, won three battles in succession, killed the Jin officer Gao the Grand Guardian, and took more than seventy chieftains prisoner.

sentences.zh: 光世等皆不敢前，飛師孤力寡，楚遂陷。

translations.literal: Guangshi and the others all dared not advance; Fei's army was isolated and few, and Chu fell.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi and the others would not advance; Yue Fei's force stood alone and Chu fell.

sentences.zh: 詔飛還守通、泰，有旨可守即守，如不可，但以沙洲保護百姓，伺便掩擊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fei back to guard Tong and Tai, with instructions that where defense was possible he should hold, and where not, he should only use the sandbanks to protect the people and await chances for surprise attacks.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered back to guard Tong and Tai: hold where holding was possible; otherwise shelter the people on the sandbanks and strike when chance offered.

sentences.zh: 飛以泰無險可恃，退保柴墟，戰于南霸橋，金大敗。

translations.literal: Fei, finding Taizhou had no defensible terrain to rely on, withdrew to hold Chaixu; fighting at Nanba Bridge, he inflicted a great defeat on the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Taizhou indefensible, he withdrew to Chaixu, fought at Nanba Bridge, and routed the Jin.

sentences.zh: 渡百姓於沙上，飛以精騎二百殿，金兵不敢近。

translations.literal: He ferried the people onto the sandbanks; Fei with two hundred elite horsemen brought up the rear, and the Jin troops dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: He ferried the people onto the sandbanks while two hundred elite horsemen under his command held the rear; the Jin dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 飛以泰州失守待罪。

translations.literal: Fei awaited punishment for the loss of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei offered himself for punishment over the loss of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 張用寇江西，用亦相人，飛以書諭之曰：「吾與汝同里，南薰門、鐵路步之戰，皆汝所悉。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong raided Jiangxi; Yong was also a man of Xiang. Fei sent a letter instructing him, saying, "You and I are from the same home district; the battles at Nanxun Gate and Tielu Bu—you know them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong raided Jiangxi. A fellow townsman of Yue Fei's, Yong received a letter from him that read: "You and I come from the same place—you remember the fighting at Nanxun Gate and Tielu Bu.

sentences.zh: 今吾在此，欲戰則出，不戰則降。

translations.literal: Now that I am here, if you wish to fight, come out; if not, surrender."
translations.idiomatic: I am here now. If you want a fight, come out; if not, surrender."

sentences.zh: 」用得書曰：「果吾父也。

translations.literal: " Yong received the letter and said, "He truly is my elder from home.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yong read it he exclaimed, "It truly is our elder from home.

sentences.zh: 」遂降。

translations.literal: " And so he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " And so he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 江、淮平，俊奏飛功第一，加神武右軍副統制，留洪州，彈壓盜賊，授親衞大夫、建州觀察使。

translations.literal: When the Jiang and Huai regions were pacified, Jun memorialized Fei's merit as foremost; he was promoted to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Right Army of Divine Martiality, left at Hongzhou to suppress bandits, and appointed Court Grandee of the Imperial Guard and Military Commissioner of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiang and Huai regions were pacified, Zhang Jun ranked Yue Fei's achievements first. He was promoted deputy commander-in-chief of the Right Army of Divine Martiality, left at Hongzhou to suppress bandits, and made Court Grandee of the Imperial Guard and Military Commissioner of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 建寇范汝為陷邵武，江西安撫李回檄飛分兵保建昌軍及撫州，飛遣人以「岳」字幟植城門，賊望見，相戒勿犯。

translations.literal: The Jian bandit Fan Ruwei seized Shaowu. Li Hui, Pacification Commissioner of Jiangxi, ordered Fei by dispatch to divide his troops to guard Jianchang Prefecture and Fuzhou. Fei sent men to plant banners bearing the character "Yue" at the city gates; the bandits saw them and warned one another not to trespass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jian bandit Fan Ruwei took Shaowu, Li Hui, the Jiangxi pacification commissioner, ordered Yue Fei to detach troops to hold Jianchang Prefecture and Fuzhou. He had banners emblazoned with the character "Yue" posted at the gates; bandits who saw them warned one another to keep away.

sentences.zh: 賊黨姚達、饒青逼建昌，飛遣王萬、徐慶討擒之。

translations.literal: The bandit partisans Yao Da and Rao Qing pressed Jianchang; Fei sent Wang Wan and Xu Qing to campaign against them and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit lieutenants Yao Da and Rao Qing threatened Jianchang; Yue Fei sent Wang Wan and Xu Qing to defeat and capture them.

sentences.zh: 升神武副軍都統制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander-in-Chief of the Deputy Army of Divine Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted commander-in-chief of the Deputy Army of Divine Martiality.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊曹成擁衆十餘萬，由江西歷湖湘，據道、賀二州。

translations.literal: In the second year, the bandit Cao Cheng mustered a host of more than a hundred thousand, passed through Jiangxi and Hunan, and held Dao and He Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the bandit chief Cao Cheng led more than a hundred thousand men from Jiangxi through Hunan and seized Dao and He prefectures.

sentences.zh: 命飛權知潭州，兼權荊湖東路安撫都總管，付金字牌、黃旗招成。

translations.literal: Fei was ordered to serve as acting prefect of Tanzhou and concurrently acting Grand Pacification Commissioner of the Eastern Circuit of Jinghu, and was given a golden tally tablet and yellow banner to summon Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was appointed acting prefect of Tanzhou and concurrently acting grand pacification commissioner of the Eastern Jinghu Circuit, with a golden tally tablet and yellow banner to summon Cheng to surrender.

sentences.zh: 成聞飛將至，驚曰：「岳家軍來矣。

translations.literal: When Cheng heard Fei was about to arrive, he said in alarm, "The Yue Family Army is coming.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yue Fei was on his way, Cheng exclaimed in alarm, "The Yue Family Army is coming!

sentences.zh: 」即分道而遁。

translations.literal: " At once he split his forces and fled by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately split his forces and fled by different routes.

sentences.zh: 飛至茶陵，奉詔招之，成不從。

translations.literal: Fei reached Chaling and, by imperial order, sought to win Cheng over, but Cheng would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei reached Chaling and tried to win Cheng over by imperial order, but Cheng refused.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「比年多命招安，故盜力強則肆暴，力屈則就招，苟不略加剿除，蠭起之衆未可遽殄。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "In recent years orders for pacification through enlistment have been many, so when bandits are strong they rampage, and when their strength fails they accept enlistment; if we do not somewhat suppress and eliminate them, masses rising like swarming bees cannot be quickly exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei memorialized: "In recent years the court has relied too much on offers of amnesty: bandits raid when strong and surrender when weak. Unless we suppress them firmly, swarms of rebels cannot be wiped out quickly.

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: " Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 飛入賀州境，得成諜者，縛之帳下。

translations.literal: Fei entered He Prefecture territory, captured one of Cheng's spies, and bound him below the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Entering He Prefecture, Yue Fei captured one of Cheng's spies and had him bound in camp.

sentences.zh: 飛出帳調兵食，吏曰：「糧盡矣，奈何？

translations.literal: Fei went outside the tent to arrange troops and supplies; an officer said, "Grain is exhausted—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei stepped outside to arrange rations; an officer said, "Our grain is gone—what now?

sentences.zh: 」飛陽曰：「姑反茶陵。

translations.literal: " Fei said openly, "For now return to Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei said loudly, for all to hear, "We will withdraw to Chaling for now.

sentences.zh: 」已而顧諜若失意狀，頓足而入，陰令逸之。

translations.literal: " Then, looking back at the spy as if distressed, he stamped his foot and reentered, secretly ordering that he be released.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he glanced at the spy as though in dismay, stamped his foot, and went back inside—while secretly ordering the man released.

sentences.zh: 諜歸告成，成大喜，期翌日來追。

translations.literal: The spy returned and reported to Cheng; Cheng was greatly pleased and set the next day to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The spy reported back to Cheng, who rejoiced and planned to pursue the next day.

sentences.zh: 飛命士蓐食，潛趨繞嶺，未明，已至太平場，破其砦。

translations.literal: Fei ordered the soldiers to eat at dawn without cooking, secretly rushed by a route around the ridge, and before daylight had already reached Taiping Post and stormed his fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei had his men take a cold meal before dawn, stole around the ridge, and before daybreak reached Taiping Post and smashed Cao Cheng's camp.

sentences.zh: 成據險拒飛，飛麾兵掩擊，賊大潰。

translations.literal: Cheng held defensible terrain to resist Fei; Fei waved his troops forward in a surprise attack and the bandits broke in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng made a stand in rough terrain; Yue Fei launched a surprise assault and the bandits broke completely.

sentences.zh: 成走據北藏嶺、上梧關，遣將迎戰，飛不陣而鼓，士爭奮，奪二隘據之。

translations.literal: Cheng fled to hold Beizang Ridge and Shangwu Pass, sent generals to meet the attack; Fei had drums beaten without forming ranks, soldiers vied in zeal, and seized the two defiles and held them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng fell back to Beizang Ridge and Shangwu Pass and sent officers to fight. Yue Fei ordered drums without waiting to form ranks; his men surged forward and seized both passes.

sentences.zh: 成又自桂嶺置砦至北藏嶺，連控隘道，親以衆十餘萬守蓬頭嶺。

translations.literal: Cheng further from Guiling to Beizang Ridge set camps in a chain controlling the defile paths, and personally with a host of more than a hundred thousand guarded Pengtou Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng strung camps from Guiling to Beizang Ridge, blocking every pass, and personally held Pengtou Ridge with more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 飛部才八千，一鼓登嶺，破其衆，成奔連州。

translations.literal: Fei's force numbered only eight thousand; at one drumbeat they climbed the ridge, broke his host, and Cheng fled to Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei had only eight thousand men. At a single drum roll they stormed the ridge, routed the enemy, and Cheng fled toward Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 飛謂張憲等曰：「成黨散去，追而殺之，則脅從者可憫，縱之則復聚為盜。

translations.literal: Fei said to Zhang Xian and the others, "When Cheng's partisans scatter, if we pursue and kill them, those coerced to follow will be pitiable; if we release them, they will gather again as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei told Zhang Xian and the others: "Cheng's followers are scattering. Hunt them down and kill them, and we destroy men who were forced to follow him; let them go and they will band together again.

sentences.zh: 今遣若等誅其酋而撫其衆，慎勿妄殺，累主上保民之仁。

translations.literal: Now I send you to execute their chieftains and pacify their masses—take care not to kill recklessly and burden Our Lord's benevolence in protecting the people.
translations.idiomatic: I send you to cut down the leaders and win over the rest. Do not kill indiscriminately and betray the emperor's wish to protect the people.

sentences.zh: 」於是憲自賀、連，徐慶自邵、道，王貴自郴、桂，招降者二萬，與飛會連州。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xian from He and Lian, Xu Qing from Shao and Dao, and Wang Gui from Chen and Gui won over twenty thousand who surrendered, and joined Fei at Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Xian swept He and Lian, Xu Qing Shaozhou and Daozhou, Wang Gui Chenzhou and Guizhou; twenty thousand surrendered and joined Yue Fei at Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 進兵追成，成走宣撫司降。

translations.literal: Advancing in pursuit of Cheng, Cheng fled and surrendered to a Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the pursuit, they drove Cheng to surrender to the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 時以盛夏行師瘴地，撫循有方，士無一人死癘者，嶺表平。

translations.literal: It was midsummer and the army marched through malarial country; care and comfort were rightly applied, and not one soldier died of pestilence; the region south of the passes was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Though it was midsummer in malarial country, his care of the troops was so thorough that not one man died of fever, and the Lingnan region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 授武安軍承宣使，屯江州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Martial Peace Army and encamped at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Martial Peace Army and stationed at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甫入境，安撫李回檄飛捕劇賊馬友、郝通、劉忠、李通、李宗亮、張式，皆平之。

translations.literal: Hardly had he entered the territory when Pacification Commissioner Li Hui dispatched Fei to capture fierce bandits Ma You, Hao Tong, Liu Zhong, Li Tong, Li Zongliang, and Zhang Shi; he pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely entered the circuit when Li Hui ordered him to capture the notorious bandits Ma You, Hao Tong, Liu Zhong, Li Tong, Li Zongliang, and Zhang Shi—all were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 三年春，召赴行在。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was summoned to the temporary capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 江西宣諭劉大中奏：「飛兵有紀律，人恃以安，今赴行在，恐盜復起。

translations.literal: Liu Dazhong, Imperial Envoy to Jiangxi, memorialized: "Fei's troops are disciplined and the people rely on them for security; if he now goes to the temporary capital, I fear bandits will rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dazhong, the imperial envoy to Jiangxi, memorialized: "Yue Fei's troops are disciplined and the people depend on them for safety. If he leaves for court, bandits may rise again.

sentences.zh: 」不果行。

translations.literal: " The journey did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not go.

sentences.zh: 時虔、吉盜連兵寇掠循、梅、廣、惠、英、韶、南雄、南安、建昌、汀、邵武諸郡，帝乃專命飛平之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits from Gan and Ji joined forces to raid and plunder the prefectures of Xun, Mei, Guang, Hui, Ying, Shao, Nanxiong, Nan'an, Jianchang, Ting, and Shaowu; the Emperor then specially ordered Fei to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits from Ganzhou and Jizhou were raiding Xunzhou, Meizhou, Guangzhou, Huizhou, Yingde, Shaozhou, Nanxiong, Nan'an, Jianchang, Tingzhou, Shaowu, and other prefectures; the emperor charged Yue Fei alone to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 飛至虔州，固石洞賊彭友悉衆至雩都迎戰，躍馬馳突，飛麾兵即馬上擒之，餘酋退保固石洞。

translations.literal: Fei reached Ganzhou; Peng You, bandit of Gushi Cave, brought his entire force to Yudu to meet him in battle and charged on horseback; Fei waved his troops forward and seized him right from the saddle; the remaining chieftains withdrew to hold Gushi Cave.
translations.idiomatic: At Ganzhou, Peng You of Gushi Cave marched his whole force to Yudu to fight. Leaping on horseback to charge, he was seized by Yue Fei's men before he could break through; the other chiefs fled back to Gushi Cave.

sentences.zh: 洞高峻環水，止一徑可入。

translations.literal: The cave was lofty and steep, ringed by water; only one path gave access.
translations.idiomatic: The stronghold stood high above the water with only a single narrow path in.

sentences.zh: 飛列騎山下，令皆持滿，黎明，遣死士疾馳登山，賊衆亂，棄山而下，騎兵圍之。

translations.literal: Fei lined cavalry below the mountain and ordered all to hold arrows nocked; at dawn he sent death-defying warriors galloping up the mountain; the bandit multitude was thrown into disorder, fled down the mountain, and the horsemen encircled them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei drew up cavalry at the foot of the hill with bows fully drawn. At dawn he sent picked men racing up the slope; the bandits panicked and fled downhill into a ring of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 賊呼丐命，飛令勿殺，受其降。

translations.literal: The bandits cried out begging for their lives; Fei ordered that they not be killed and accepted their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They cried for mercy; Yue Fei forbade killing and accepted their surrender.

sentences.zh: 授徐慶等方略，捕諸郡餘賊，皆破降之。

translations.literal: He entrusted Xu Qing and others with tactics to capture remnant bandits of the various prefectures; all were defeated and made to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He detailed Xu Qing and others to hunt down remaining bandits in the prefectures—all were defeated or persuaded to surrender.

sentences.zh: 初，以隆祐震驚之故，密旨令飛屠虔城。

translations.literal: At first, because of Empress Dowager Longyou's terror, a secret order directed Fei to massacre the city of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first, shaken by the shock to Empress Dowager Longyou, the court secretly ordered Yue Fei to slaughter Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 飛請誅首惡而赦脅從，不許；

translations.literal: Fei begged to execute the chief evildoers and pardon those coerced to follow; permission was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei asked to execute the ringleaders and pardon those forced to follow; the court refused;

sentences.zh: 請至三四，帝乃曲赦。

translations.literal: after three or four petitions, the Emperor at last granted a partial amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: only after three or four appeals did the emperor grant a limited pardon.

sentences.zh: 人感其德，繪像祠之。

translations.literal: The people were grateful for his virtue and painted his portrait to enshrine him.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for his mercy, the people painted his image and worshipped him in a shrine.

sentences.zh: 餘寇高聚、張成犯袁州，飛遣王貴平之。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits Gao Ju and Zhang Cheng invaded Yuanzhou; Fei sent Wang Gui to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining bandits Gao Ju and Zhang Cheng attacked Yuanzhou; Yue Fei sent Wang Gui to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 秋，入見，帝手書「精忠岳飛」字，製旗以賜之。

translations.literal: In autumn he entered audience; the Emperor personally wrote the characters "Utmost Loyalty Yue Fei," had a banner made, and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he attended court; the emperor personally wrote the four characters "Utmost Loyalty Yue Fei" and had a banner made and conferred on him.

sentences.zh: 授鎮南軍承宣使、江南西路沿江制置使，又改神武後軍都統制，仍制置使，李山、吳全、吳錫、李橫、牛皐皆隸焉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Army Pacifying the South and Commissioner of the Jiangxi West Circuit River Defense; then changed to Commander-in-Chief of the Rear Army of Divine Martiality while retaining the commissioner post; Li Shan, Wu Quan, Wu Xi, Li Heng, and Niu Gao were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Army Pacifying the South and river-defense commissioner for western Jiangxi, then reassigned as commander-in-chief of the Rear Army of Divine Martiality while retaining his commissioner title; Li Shan, Wu Quan, Wu Xi, Li Heng, and Niu Gao all came under his command.

sentences.zh: 偽齊遣李成挾金人入侵，破襄陽、唐、鄧、隨、郢諸州及信陽軍，湖寇楊么亦與偽齊通，欲順流而下，李成又欲自江西陸行，趨兩浙與么會。

translations.literal: The puppet Qi state sent Li Cheng at the head of Jin troops to invade, seizing Xiangyang, Tang, Deng, Suizhou, Ying, and other prefectures and Xinyang Prefecture; the lake bandit Yang Mo also communicated with puppet Qi, intending to descend with the current, while Cheng also wished to march overland from Jiangxi toward the two Zhe circuits to join Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Puppet Qi sent Li Cheng with Jin allies to invade, capturing Xiangyang, Tangzhou, Dengzhou, Suizhou, Yingzhou, and Xinyang Prefecture. The lake bandit Yang Mo coordinated with Puppet Qi for a descent downriver while Li Cheng planned to march overland from Jiangxi into the two Zhe circuits to link up with him.

sentences.zh: 帝命飛為之備。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Fei to make preparations against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yue Fei to prepare against them.

sentences.zh: 四年，除兼荊南、鄂岳州制置使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed concurrently Commissioner of Jingnan and the E-Yue prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was additionally appointed commissioner for Jingnan and the E-Yue prefectures.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「襄陽等六郡為恢復中原基本，今當先取六郡，以除心膂之病。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "The six prefectures including Xiangyang are the foundation for recovering the Central Plains; we should now first take the six prefectures to remove the disease at heart and vitals.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei memorialized: "The six prefectures including Xiangyang are the base for recovering the north. We must seize them first and cut out the enemy's heart.

sentences.zh: 李成遠遁，然後加兵湖湘，以殄羣盜。

translations.literal: When Li Cheng has fled far off, then add troops to Hunan and eliminate the bandit hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Cheng is driven far off, we can reinforce Hunan and wipe out the bandits.

sentences.zh: 」帝以諭趙鼎，鼎曰：「知上流利害，無如飛者。

translations.literal: " The Emperor communicated this to Zhao Ding; Ding said, "In knowing the advantages and harms of the upper reaches of the rivers, none match Fei.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor showed the memorial to Zhao Ding, who said, "No one understands the upper rivers as well as Yue Fei.

sentences.zh: 」遂授黃復州、漢陽軍、德安府制置使。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed Commissioner of Huangzhou, Fuzhou, Hanyang Prefecture, and De'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei was appointed commissioner for Huangzhou, Fuzhou, Hanyang Prefecture, and De'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 飛渡江中流，顧幕屬曰：「飛不擒賊，不涉此江。

translations.literal: Fei crossed midstream on the Yangzi and, turning to his staff, said, "If Fei does not capture the bandits, he will not cross this river again.
translations.idiomatic: Midstream on the Yangzi, Yue Fei turned to his staff and said, "If I do not capture the enemy, I shall not cross this river again.

sentences.zh: 」抵郢州城下，偽將京超號「萬人敵」，乘城拒飛。

translations.literal: " He reached beneath the walls of Ying Prefecture; the puppet general Jing Chao, styled "Foe of Ten Thousand Men," mounted the walls to resist Fei.
translations.idiomatic: " He reached Ying Prefecture; the enemy general Jing Chao, called "Match for Ten Thousand," held the walls against him.

sentences.zh: 飛鼓衆而登，超投崖死，復郢州，遣張憲、徐慶復隨州。

translations.literal: Fei beat the drums and the troops scaled the wall; Chao threw himself off the cliff and died; Ying Prefecture was recovered, and Zhang Xian and Xu Qing were sent to recover Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei stormed the walls at drumbeat; Jing Chao leaped to his death from the cliff. Ying Prefecture was retaken and Zhang Xian and Xu Qing recovered Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 飛趣襄陽，李成迎戰，左臨襄江，飛笑曰：「步兵利險阻，騎兵利平曠。

translations.literal: Fei hurried to Xiangyang; Li Cheng came out to fight with the Xiang River on his left; Fei laughed and said, "Infantry excel in rugged defiles, cavalry excel on open ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei pressed on to Xiangyang. Li Cheng met him with the Xiang River on his left flank. Yue Fei smiled and said, "Infantry fight best in tight ground, cavalry on open ground.

sentences.zh: 成左列騎江岸，右列步平地，雖衆十萬何能為。

translations.literal: Cheng has cavalry arrayed on the left along the riverbank and infantry on the right on level ground—though he has a hundred thousand, what can he do?
translations.idiomatic: He has cavalry on the river side and foot soldiers on open ground—even with a hundred thousand men, what can he do?

sentences.zh: 」舉鞭指王貴曰：「爾以長槍步卒擊其騎兵。

translations.literal: " Raising his whip he pointed at Wang Gui and said, "You with long-spear foot soldiers strike his cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised his whip toward Wang Gui: "Take your long-spear foot soldiers against his cavalry.

sentences.zh: 」指牛皐曰：「爾以騎兵擊其步卒。

translations.literal: " He pointed at Niu Gao and said, "You with cavalry strike his foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " To Niu Gao: "Take your cavalry against his foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」合戰，馬應槍而斃，後騎皆擁入江，步卒死者無數，成夜遁，復襄陽。

translations.literal: " They joined battle; horses fell at the spears and died, the rear horsemen all were crowded into the river, foot soldiers died without number, Cheng fled by night, and Xiangyang was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " The armies clashed; horses fell to the spears, ridden men were shoved into the river, foot soldiers died in heaps. Li Cheng fled by night and Xiangyang was recovered.

sentences.zh: 劉豫益成兵屯新野，飛與王萬夾擊之，連破其衆。

translations.literal: Liu Yu reinforced Cheng's troops and encamped at Xinye; Fei with Wang Wan attacked from both sides and repeatedly broke his host.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu reinforced Li Cheng at Xinye; Yue Fei and Wang Wan struck from both sides and routed them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「金賊所愛惟子女金帛，志已驕惰；

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "What the Jin bandits love is only sons and daughters, gold and silks; their will is already arrogant and indolent;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei memorialized: "The Jin care only for loot and comfort; they have grown arrogant and slack;

sentences.zh: 劉豫僭偽，人心終不忘宋。

translations.literal: Liu Yu usurps falsely, yet in men's hearts they never forget Song.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's regime is a usurpation, but men's hearts still turn to Song.

sentences.zh: 如以精兵二十萬，直擣中原，恢復故疆，誠易為力。

translations.literal: If with an elite army of two hundred thousand we strike straight at the Central Plains and recover the old territory, it truly would be easy in effort.
translations.idiomatic: Send two hundred thousand picked troops straight into the Central Plains and recovering our old borders would be well within our power.

sentences.zh: 襄陽、隨、郢地皆膏腴，苟行營田，其利為厚。

translations.literal: The lands of Xiangyang, Suizhou, and Ying are all rich soil; if we establish military farms, the profit will be great.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang, Suizhou, and Yingzhou sit on rich land; military farming there would yield great profit.

sentences.zh: 臣候糧足，即過江北剿戮敵兵。

translations.literal: Your subject waits until grain is sufficient, then will cross north of the river to slay and destroy the enemy troops.
translations.idiomatic: When our grain is ready, I will cross the river and destroy the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」時方重深入之舉，而營田之議自是興矣。

translations.literal: " At the time the court was just then placing weight on deep thrusts, and from this the proposal for military colonies arose.
translations.idiomatic: " The court was already weighing bold northern offensives, and from this time the debate over military colonies began.

sentences.zh: 進兵鄧州，成與金將劉合孛堇列砦拒飛。

translations.literal: Advancing to Deng Prefecture, Cheng with the Jin general Liu Hebejin set camps in array to resist Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Dengzhou, Li Cheng and the Jin general Liu Hebejin encamped to block him.

sentences.zh: 飛遣王貴、張憲掩擊，賊衆大潰，劉合孛堇僅以身免。

translations.literal: Fei sent Wang Gui and Zhang Xian in a surprise attack; the bandit host broke in great disorder, and Liu Hebejin barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sent Wang Gui and Zhang Xian in a flank attack; the enemy collapsed and Liu Hebejin barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 賊黨高仲退保鄧城，飛引兵一鼓拔之，擒高仲，復鄧州。

translations.literal: The bandit partisan Gao Zhong withdrew to hold Deng city; Fei led troops and at one drum roll stormed it, captured Gao Zhong, and recovered Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit lieutenant Gao Zhong fell back to Deng city; Yue Fei took it at the first assault, captured Gao Zhong, and recovered Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，喜曰：「朕素聞岳飛行軍有紀律，未知能破敵如此。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and said joyfully, "We have long heard that Yue Fei's marching has discipline; We did not know he could break the enemy like this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced: "I have long heard Yue Fei keeps strict discipline on campaign—I did not know he could smash the enemy like this.

sentences.zh: 」又復唐州、信陽軍。

translations.literal: " Tang Prefecture and Xinyang Prefecture were also recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " Tangzhou and Xinyang Prefecture were also retaken.

sentences.zh: 襄漢平，飛辭制置使，乞委重臣經畫荊襄，不許。

translations.literal: When Xiang and Han were pacified, Fei resigned the commissioner post, begging that a senior minister be entrusted to plan Jing and Xiang; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: With the Xiang-Han region pacified, Yue Fei tried to resign his commissioner title and asked that a senior minister take charge of Jing-Xiang; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎奏：「湖北鄂、岳最為上流要害，乞令飛屯鄂、岳，不惟江西藉其聲勢，湖、廣、江、浙亦獲安妥。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding memorialized: "In Hubei, E and Yue are most the vital points of the upper reaches; I beg that Fei be ordered to encamp at E and Yue—not only will Jiangxi rely on his prestige, but Hunan, Guang, Jiang, and Zhe will also gain security.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding memorialized: "Ezhou and Yuezhou in Hubei guard the upper Yangzi. Station Yue Fei there and Jiangxi gains his protection, while Hunan, Guang, Jiang, and Zhe all grow safer.

sentences.zh: 」乃以隨、郢、唐、鄧、信陽並為襄陽府路隸飛，飛移屯鄂，授清遠軍節度使、湖北路、荊、襄、潭州制置使，封武昌縣開國子。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Suizhou, Ying, Tang, Deng, and Xinyang were all placed under Xiangyang Prefecture Circuit under Fei; Fei moved his encampment to E, was appointed Military Governor of the Qingyuan Army and Commissioner of Hubei Circuit and the Jing, Xiang, and Tan prefectures, and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: " Suizhou, Yingzhou, Tangzhou, Dengzhou, and Xinyang were folded into the Xiangyang circuit under his command. He moved to Ezhou, became military governor of the Qingyuan Army and commissioner for Hubei and the Jing-Xiang-Tan region, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuchang County.

sentences.zh: 兀朮、劉豫合兵圍廬州，帝手札命飛解圍，提兵趨廬，偽齊已驅甲騎五千逼城。

translations.literal: Wuzhu and Liu Yu combined forces to besiege Luzhou; the Emperor wrote by hand ordering Fei to relieve the siege; Fei led troops toward Lu; puppet Qi had already driven five thousand armored horsemen to press the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu and Liu Yu besieged Luzhou; the emperor's personal note ordered Yue Fei to the rescue. He marched for Lu while Puppet Qi already had five thousand armored cavalry at the walls.

sentences.zh: 飛張「岳」字旗與「精忠」旗，金兵一戰而潰，廬州平。

translations.literal: Fei raised the banner with the character "Yue" and the "Utmost Loyalty" banner; the Jin troops broke at one battle, and Luzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei unfurled his "Yue" banner and his "Utmost Loyalty" banner; the Jin broke at the first clash and Luzhou was saved.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「襄陽等六郡人戶闕牛、糧，乞量給官錢，免官私逋負，州縣官以招集流亡為殿最。」

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "The households of the six prefectures including Xiangyang lack oxen and grain; I beg that official funds be allotted in measure, public and private arrears be remitted, and prefectural and county officials be judged for promotion and demotion by how well they gather in the displaced."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei memorialized: "Households in the six Xiangyang prefectures lack oxen and grain. Grant official funds in proportion, cancel public and private debts, and rate local officials on how well they bring back refugees."

sentences.zh: 五年，入覲，封母國夫人；

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered audience; his mother was enfeoffed as Lady of the State;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he attended court; his mother was enfeoffed as Lady of the State;

sentences.zh: 授飛鎮寧、崇信軍節度使，湖北路、荊襄潭州制置使，進封武昌郡開國侯；

translations.literal: Fei was appointed Military Governor of the Armies Pacifying Tranquility and Honoring Trust, Commissioner of Hubei Circuit and the Jing-Xiang-Tan prefectures, and advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Wuchang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was made military governor of the Pacifying Tranquility and Honoring Trust armies and commissioner for Hubei and Jing-Xiang-Tan, raised to Marquis of Wuchang Commandery;

sentences.zh: 又除荊湖南北、襄陽路制置使，神武後軍都統制，命招捕楊么。

translations.literal: additionally appointed Commissioner of the Northern and Southern Hunan and Xiangyang circuits and Commander-in-Chief of the Rear Army of Divine Martiality, and ordered to summon and capture Yang Mo.
translations.idiomatic: and additionally made commissioner for northern and southern Hunan and the Xiangyang circuit and commander-in-chief of the Rear Army of Divine Martiality, with orders to capture Yang Mo.

sentences.zh: 飛所部皆西北人，不習水戰，飛曰：「兵何常，顧用之何如耳。

translations.literal: Fei's command were all northwesterners, unskilled in river warfare; Fei said, "What is constant about troops? It all depends on how they are used.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei's troops were mostly northwesterners, unused to fighting on water. He said, "Soldiers are what you make of them—it all depends on how you use them.

sentences.zh: 」先遣使招諭之。

translations.literal: " First he sent envoys to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: " First he sent envoys to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 賊黨黃佐曰：「岳節使號令如山，若與之敵，萬無生理，不如往降。

translations.literal: The bandit partisan Huang Zuo said, "Commissioner Yue's commands are immovable as a mountain; if we oppose him, there is no way to live—better to go and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit lieutenant Huang Zuo said, "Commissioner Yue's orders stand like a mountain. Fight him and we cannot survive—we should surrender.

sentences.zh: 節使誠信，必善遇我。

translations.literal: The Commissioner is sincere and trustworthy; he will surely treat us well.
translations.idiomatic: He is true to his word and will treat us well.

sentences.zh: 」遂降。

translations.literal: " And so he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " And so they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 飛表授佐武義大夫，單騎按其部，拊佐背曰：「子知逆順者。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized to appoint Zuo as Grand Master of Martial Righteousness, rode alone to inspect his unit, and patting Zuo's back said, "You understand what is rebellious and what is compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei petitioned to appoint Huang Zuo Grand Master of Martial Righteousness, rode alone through his ranks, and clapped him on the back: "You know which way the tide runs.

sentences.zh: 果能立功，封侯豈足道？

translations.literal: If you can truly achieve merit, would enfeoffment as marquis be worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: If you win real merit, a marquisate will be the least of your rewards.

sentences.zh: 欲復遣子至湖中，視其可乘者擒之，可勸者招之，如何？

translations.literal: I wish again to send you to the lake region—to seize those that can be seized, and win over those that can be won. What say you?
translations.idiomatic: I want to send you back to the lakes—seize those we can seize, win over those we can persuade. Will you go?

sentences.zh: 」佐感泣，誓以死報。

translations.literal: " Zuo wept with emotion and swore to repay with his life.
translations.idiomatic: " Huang Zuo wept and pledged his life in return.

sentences.zh: 時張浚以都督軍事至潭，參政席益與浚語，疑飛玩寇，欲以聞。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun came to Tan as overall military commander; Vice Administrator Xi Yi spoke with Jun, suspecting that Fei was toying with the bandits, and wished to report this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun had arrived at Tanzhou as overall commander. Vice Administrator Xi Yi told him he suspected Yue Fei was deliberately indulging the bandits and wanted to report it.

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「岳侯，忠孝人也，兵有深機，胡可易言？

translations.literal: Jun said, "Lord Yue is a man of loyalty and filial piety; in military affairs there are deep stratagems—how can one speak of them lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun said, "Lord Yue is a man of loyalty and devotion. War has its deep stratagems—how can you speak so casually?

sentences.zh: 」益慙而止。

translations.literal: " Yi was ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi Yi withdrew, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 黃佐襲周倫砦，殺倫，擒其統制陳貴等。

translations.literal: Huang Zuo assaulted Zhou Lun's fort, killed Lun, and captured his regiment commander Chen Gui and others.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zuo stormed Zhou Lun's camp, killed Lun, and captured regiment commander Chen Gui and others.

sentences.zh: 飛上其功，遷武功大夫。

translations.literal: Fei reported his merit upward; he was transferred to Grand Master of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei reported the victory and Huang Zuo was promoted to Grand Master of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 統制任士安不稟王𤫉令，軍以此無功。

translations.literal: Regiment commander Ren Shi'an did not obey Wang Yuan's order, and on this account the army achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Regiment commander Ren Shi'an disobeyed Wang Yuan's order, and the operation failed.

sentences.zh: 飛鞭士安使餌賊，曰：「三日賊不平，斬汝。

translations.literal: Fei had Shi'an whipped and sent him to bait the bandits, saying, "If the bandits are not pacified in three days, you will be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei had Shi'an flogged and sent him to lure the enemy, saying, "If the bandits are not suppressed within three days, you die.

sentences.zh: 」士安宣言：「岳太尉兵二十萬至矣。

translations.literal: " Shi'an proclaimed: "Grand Marshal Yue's army of two hundred thousand has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shi'an spread the word: "Lord Yue has brought two hundred thousand men!"

sentences.zh: 」賊見止士安軍，併力攻之。

translations.literal: " The bandits, seeing only Shi'an's army, combined their strength and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, seeing only Shi'an's force, massed together and attacked.

sentences.zh: 飛設伏，士安戰急，伏四起擊賊，賊走。

translations.literal: Fei set ambushes; Shi'an fought fiercely; the ambushers rose on four sides and struck the bandits, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei had laid ambushes. When Shi'an's fight grew desperate, the hidden troops struck from every side and the bandits broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 會召浚還防秋，飛袖小圖示浚，浚欲俟來年議之。

translations.literal: Just then Jun was summoned back for autumn defense; Fei drew a small map from his sleeve and showed it to Jun, but Jun wished to wait until the next year to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was then recalled for the autumn defense. Yue Fei pulled a small map from his sleeve to show him, but Zhang Jun wanted to put the matter off until the following year.

sentences.zh: 飛曰：「已有定畫，都督能少留，不八日可破賊。

translations.literal: Fei said, "There is already a fixed plan; if the Commissioner can stay a little longer, the bandits can be broken in fewer than eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei said, "The plan is already set. If you can stay a few days longer, the bandits will be broken in under eight."

sentences.zh: 」浚曰：「何言之易？

translations.literal: " Jun said, "Why do you speak so lightly?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jun said, "That sounds too easy."

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「王四廂以王師攻水寇則難，飛以水寇攻水寇則易。

translations.literal: " Fei said, "For Wang Siboxiang to use the imperial army against water bandits is hard; for Fei to use water bandits against water bandits is easy.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei said, "It is hard for Wang Siboxiang to take imperial troops against lake pirates—but easy for me to set pirate against pirate."

sentences.zh: 水戰我短彼長，以所短攻所長，所以難。

translations.literal: In water combat our weakness is their strength; to use what is weak against what is strong is why it is hard.
translations.idiomatic: On water we are weak where they are strong; pitting weakness against strength is what makes it hard.

sentences.zh: 若因敵將用敵兵，奪其手足之助，離其腹心之託，使孤立，而後以王師乘之，八日之內，當俘諸酋。

translations.literal: If we employ the enemy's generals and use the enemy's troops, seize the help of their hands and feet, sever the reliance of their heart and vitals, leave them isolated, and then let the imperial army press them, within eight days we should capture the chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Use their own commanders and their own men. Cut off their arms and legs, tear out their heart—leave them isolated—then let the imperial army strike. Within eight days we will have their chieftains in chains.

sentences.zh: 」浚許之。

translations.literal: " Jun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 飛遂如鼎州。

translations.literal: Fei then went to Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei then proceeded to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 黃佐招楊欽來降，飛喜曰：「楊欽驍悍，既降，賊腹心潰矣。

translations.literal: Huang Zuo won over Yang Qin to come and surrender; Fei said joyfully, "Yang Qin is fierce and bold; once he has surrendered, the bandits' heart and vitals will collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zuo persuaded Yang Qin to defect. Yue Fei rejoiced: "Yang Qin is their fiercest fighter. Once he comes over, the rebels' core will crumble."

sentences.zh: 」表授欽武義大夫，禮遇甚厚，乃復遣歸湖中。

translations.literal: " He memorialized to appoint Qin as Grand Master of Martial Righteousness, treated him with great courtesy, and then sent him back again to the lake region.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to appoint Yang Qin Grand Master of Martial Righteousness, treated him with great honor, and sent him back to the lakes.

sentences.zh: 兩日，欽說余端、劉詵等降，飛詭罵欽曰：「賊不盡降，何來也？

translations.literal: Two days later Qin persuaded Yu Duan, Liu Shen, and others to surrender; Fei feigned rebuke of Qin, saying, "The bandits have not all surrendered—why have you come?
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Yang Qin won over Yu Duan, Liu Shen, and others. Yue Fei feigned anger and berated him: "The enemy has not all surrendered—why are you back?"

sentences.zh: 」杖之，復令入湖。

translations.literal: " He had him beaten with the staff and again ordered him into the lake.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yang Qin flogged and sent him back to the lakes.

sentences.zh: 是夜，掩賊營，降其衆數萬。

translations.literal: That night he made a surprise attack on the bandit camp and caused tens of thousands of their host to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That night he stormed the rebel camp and accepted the surrender of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 么負固不服，方浮舟湖中，以輪激水，其行如飛，旁置撞竿，官舟迎之輒碎。

translations.literal: Yao held firm and would not submit; he was just then floating boats on the lake, using wheels to churn the water so that they flew like the wind, with ramming poles set on the sides—whenever government boats met them they were shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao still held out. He floated boats on the lake, paddle-wheels churning the water until they flew like wind; ramming poles lined their sides, and any government vessel that met them was smashed.

sentences.zh: 飛伐君山木為巨筏，塞諸港�，又以腐木亂草浮上流而下，擇水淺處，遣善罵者挑之，且行且罵。

translations.literal: Fei felled timber on Jun Mountain to make huge rafts and blocked the harbor mouths and channels; he also floated rotten wood and tangled grass down from upstream, chose shallow water, and sent skilled scolders to provoke them, cursing as they went.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei cut timber on Jun Mountain for giant rafts and blocked every harbor mouth and channel. He sent rotten wood and tangled grass floating downstream, then picked a shallow stretch and sent men skilled in abuse to taunt the rebels, cursing all the way.

sentences.zh: 賊怒來追，則草木壅積，舟輪礙不行。

translations.literal: The bandits, enraged, came in pursuit, but then the grass and wood piled up and the boat wheels were obstructed and could not move.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, furious, gave chase—only to find grass and timber jammed around them, their paddle-wheels fouled and stuck.

sentences.zh: 飛亟遣兵擊之，賊奔港中，為筏所拒。

translations.literal: Fei urgently sent troops to strike them; the bandits fled into the harbor mouths and were blocked by the rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei immediately sent troops after them. The rebels fled into the channels and found the rafts blocking their way.

sentences.zh: 官軍乘筏，張牛革以蔽矢石，舉巨木撞其舟，盡壞。

translations.literal: The government army boarded the rafts, stretched oxhide to shield against arrows and stones, and raised great logs to ram their boats, destroying them all.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops rode the rafts forward, oxhide stretched against arrows and stones, great logs raised to smash the rebel boats—all were wrecked.

sentences.zh: 么投水，牛皐擒斬之。

translations.literal: Yao threw himself into the water; Niu Gao captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao leaped into the water. Niu Gao seized and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 飛入賊壘，餘酋驚曰：「何神也！

translations.literal: Fei entered the bandit stronghold; the remaining chieftains cried in alarm, "What god is this!
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei entered the rebel camp. The remaining chieftains cried in terror, "What kind of god is this!"

sentences.zh: 」俱降。

translations.literal: " All surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 飛親行諸砦慰撫之，縱老弱歸田，籍少壯為軍，果八日而賊平。

translations.literal: Fei personally went through the forts to comfort and reassure them, released the old and weak to return to farming, registered the young and strong as soldiers, and indeed in eight days the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei went in person from fort to fort to reassure them, sent the old and weak back to their fields, enrolled the able-bodied as soldiers—and in eight days, as promised, the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 浚嘆曰：「岳侯神算也。

translations.literal: Jun sighed and said, "Lord Yue's divine calculation!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun marveled: "Lord Yue's calculations are uncanny."

sentences.zh: 」初，賊恃其險曰：「欲犯我者，除是飛來。

translations.literal: " Earlier the bandits, relying on their defiles, had said, "Whoever would violate us must come flying.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the rebels had boasted of their stronghold: "Whoever would take us must come flying."

sentences.zh: 」至是，人以其言為讖。

translations.literal: " At this people took their words as a fulfilled prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: Now people took those words as prophecy fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 獲賊舟千餘，鄂渚水軍為沿江之冠。

translations.literal: More than a thousand bandit boats were captured, and the Ezhou naval force became foremost along the river.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand rebel boats were captured, and the Ezhou fleet became the finest on the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 詔兼蘄、黃制置使，飛以目疾乞辭軍事，不許，加檢校少保，進封公。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him concurrently Commissioner of Qi and Huang; Fei begged to resign military affairs because of eye disease, but permission was not granted; he was promoted to Acting Junior Guardian and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner for Qizhou and Huangzhou as well. Yue Fei asked to leave military service because of eye trouble; the court refused, made him Acting Junior Guardian, and raised his rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 還軍鄂州，除荊湖南北、襄陽路招討使。

translations.literal: Returning the army to E Prefecture, he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu South and North and the Xiangyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He returned his army to Ezhou and was made pacification commissioner for Jinghu South and North and the Xiangyang circuit.

sentences.zh: 六年，太行山忠義社梁興等百餘人，慕飛義率衆來歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, more than a hundred men of the Loyalty and Righteousness Society of the Taihang Mountains, including Liang Xing, admiring Fei's righteousness, led their hosts to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, more than a hundred men of the Loyalty and Righteousness Society in the Taihang Mountains, led by Liang Xing, came over, drawn by Yue Fei's reputation.

sentences.zh: 飛入覲，面陳：「襄陽自收復後，未置監司，州縣無以按察。

translations.literal: Fei entered audience and stated face to face: "Since Xiangyang was recovered, no supervisory officials have been appointed, and the prefectures and counties have no means of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei went to court and said in person: "Since Xiangyang was recovered, no supervisory officials have been posted there, and the prefectures and counties have no one to inspect them."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，以李若虛為京西南路提舉兼轉運、提刑，又令湖北、襄陽府路自知州、通判以下賢否，許飛得自黜陟。
