translations.literal: " The Emperor assented, appointing Li Ruoxu as Intendant of the Southwest Capital Circuit concurrently as Transport Commissioner and Judicial Commissioner; he also ordered that for Hubei and the Xiangyang Prefecture Circuit, from prefects and vice-prefects downward, their worthiness be judged, and permitted Fei to dismiss and promote on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, appointing Li Ruoxu intendant for the Southwest Capital circuit with concurrent transport and judicial duties. For Hubei and the Xiangyang circuit, from prefects and vice-prefects down, Yue Fei was authorized to judge merit and dismiss or promote officials as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 張浚至江上會諸大帥，獨稱飛與韓世忠可倚大事，命飛屯襄陽，以窺中原，曰：「此君素志也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun came to the river and met the great commanders; he alone praised Fei and Han Shizhong as men on whom great affairs could be relied, ordered Fei to encamp at Xiangyang to watch the Central Plains, and said, "This has long been this lord's ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun met the great commanders on the river and singled out Yue Fei and Han Shizhong as men the dynasty could lean on. He ordered Yue Fei to encamp at Xiangyang and watch the Central Plains, saying, "That has always been your wish."

sentences.zh: 」飛移軍京西，改武勝、定國軍節度使，除宣撫副使，置司襄陽。

translations.literal: " Fei moved his army to Jingxi, was changed to Military Governor of the Wusheng and Dingguo Armies, appointed Vice Pacification Commissioner, and established his headquarters at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei moved his army to western Jing, became military governor of the Wusheng and Dingguo armies, was made vice pacification commissioner, and established headquarters at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 命往武昌調軍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Wuchang to reorganize the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Wuchang to reorganize the troops.

sentences.zh: 居母憂，降制起復，飛扶櫬還廬山，連表乞終喪，不許，累詔趣起，乃就軍。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, an edict ordered him recalled to service; Fei supported the coffin and returned to Mount Lu, repeatedly memorialized begging to complete the mourning period, permission was not granted, repeated edicts urged him to rise, and then he took up command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, an edict recalled him from mourning. Yue Fei escorted the coffin to Mount Lu and petitioned again and again to finish mourning; the court refused. Edict after edict pressed him to return, and at last he rejoined the army.

sentences.zh: 又命宣撫河東，節制河北路。

translations.literal: He was further ordered to pacify Hedong and to command Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to pacify Hedong and take command of Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 首遣王貴等攻虢州，下之，獲糧十五萬石，降其衆數萬。

translations.literal: First he sent Wang Gui and others to attack Guo Prefecture, took it, obtained one hundred fifty thousand shi of grain, and caused tens of thousands of the enemy host to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: First he sent Wang Gui and others against Guozhou. They took the city, seized a hundred fifty thousand shi of grain, and accepted the surrender of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 張浚曰：「飛措畫甚大，令已至伊、洛，則太行一帶山砦，必有應者。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun said, "Fei's planning is very grand; now that he has reached the Yi and Luo, then the mountain forts along the Taihang range will surely have men who respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun said, "Yue Fei is thinking on a grand scale. Once he reaches the Yi and Luo rivers, the mountain forts along the Taihang will answer him."

sentences.zh: 」飛遣楊再興進兵至長水縣，再戰皆捷，中原響應。

translations.literal: " Fei sent Yang Zaixing to advance to Changshui County; in two battles he was victorious, and the Central Plains responded.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sent Yang Zaixing as far as Changshui County. He won two battles in succession, and the Central Plains rose in response.

sentences.zh: 又遣人焚蔡州糧。

translations.literal: He also sent men to burn the grain at Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men to burn the grain stores at Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，劉豫遣子麟、侄猊分道寇淮西，劉光世欲舍廬州，張俊欲棄盱眙，同奏召飛以兵東下，欲使飛當其鋒，而己得退保。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Liu Yu sent his son Lin and his nephew Ni by separate routes to invade Huai West; Liu Guangshi wished to abandon Luz Prefecture, Zhang Jun wished to abandon Xuyi, and together they memorialized to summon Fei east with troops, intending to have Fei meet the enemy's spearhead while they themselves could withdraw and hold defensive positions.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Yu sent his son Liu Lin and nephew Liu Ni against Huai West by separate routes. Liu Guangshi wanted to abandon Luzhou; Zhang Jun wanted to abandon Xuyi. Both petitioned to summon Yue Fei east, hoping he would take the enemy's blow while they fell back to safety.

sentences.zh: 張浚謂：「岳飛一動，則襄漢何所制？

translations.literal: Zhang Jun said, "If Yue Fei moves, then what will hold Xiang and Han?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun argued: "If Yue Fei moves, who will hold Xiangyang and the Han?"

sentences.zh: 」力沮其議。

translations.literal: " He forcefully blocked the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked the plan with all his force.

sentences.zh: 帝慮俊、光世不足任，命飛東下。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared Jun and Guangshi were not equal to the task and ordered Fei east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi were up to the task and ordered Yue Fei east.

sentences.zh: 飛自破曹成、平楊么，凡六年，皆盛夏行師，致目疾，至是，甚；

translations.literal: From the time Fei broke Cao Cheng and pacified Yang Yao, for six years in all he had marched in the height of summer, which brought on eye disease; by now it was severe;
translations.idiomatic: Since breaking Cao Cheng and pacifying Yang Yao, Yue Fei had marched six summers in a row and ruined his eyes; by now the affliction was severe.

sentences.zh: 聞詔即日啟行，未至，麟敗。

translations.literal: on hearing the edict he set out the same day; before he arrived, Lin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the order he set out the same day. Before he arrived, Liu Lin was already beaten.

sentences.zh: 飛奏至，帝語趙鼎曰：「劉麟敗北不足喜，諸將知尊朝廷為可喜。

translations.literal: When Fei's memorial arrived, the Emperor said to Zhao Ding, "Liu Lin's defeat and flight north is not enough to rejoice in; that the generals know to honor the court is what is worth rejoicing in.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Fei's memorial arrived, the emperor told Zhao Ding, "Liu Lin's rout is nothing to celebrate. What matters is that the generals still know to obey the throne."

sentences.zh: 」遂賜札，言：「敵兵已去淮，卿不須進發，其或襄、鄧、陳、蔡有機可乘，從長措置。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he bestowed a letter saying, "The enemy troops have already left the Huai, you need not advance; if at Xiang, Deng, Chen, or Cai there is an opportunity to seize, arrange matters as you see fit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a letter: "The enemy has left the Huai—you need not march on. If openings appear at Xiangyang, Dengzhou, Chenzhou, or Caizhou, act as you judge best."

sentences.zh: 」飛乃還軍。

translations.literal: " Fei then returned the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei turned his army back.

sentences.zh: 時偽齊屯兵窺唐州，飛遣王貴、董先等攻破之，焚其營。

translations.literal: At that time the puppet Qi encamped troops watching Tang Prefecture; Fei sent Wang Gui, Dong Xian, and others to break them, and burned their camps.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet Qi had troops watching Tangzhou. Yue Fei sent Wang Gui, Dong Xian, and others to smash them and burn their camps.

sentences.zh: 奏圖蔡以取中原，不許。

translations.literal: He memorialized a plan to take Cai in order to seize the Central Plains; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to take Caizhou and push into the Central Plains. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 飛召貴等還。

translations.literal: Fei summoned Gui and the others back.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei recalled Wang Gui and the rest.

sentences.zh: 七年，入見，帝從容問曰：「卿得良馬否？

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered audience; the Emperor asked at ease, "Have you obtained fine horses?
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went to court. The emperor asked casually, "Have you found good horses?"

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「臣有二馬，日啖芻豆數斗，飲泉一斛，然非精潔則不受。

translations.literal: " Fei said, "Your subject had two horses that daily ate several dou of fodder and beans and drank a hu of spring water, yet unless it was refined and clean they would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei said, "I once had two horses. Each day they ate several dou of fodder and beans and drank a hu of spring water—but only if it was clean and choice."

sentences.zh: 介而馳，初不甚疾，比行百里始奮迅，自午至酉，猶可二百里。

translations.literal: When saddled and running, at first they were not very swift; only after a hundred li did they begin to surge forward; from noon to the hour of you they could still cover two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Saddled, they started slow. After a hundred li they gathered speed. From noon to dusk they could still run two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 褫鞍甲而不息不汗，若無事然。

translations.literal: When the saddle and armor were removed they neither panted nor sweated, as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Strip off saddle and armor and they neither panted nor sweated, as if they had done nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 此其受大而不苟取，力裕而不求逞，致遠之材也。

translations.literal: This was because they accepted much yet did not grasp greedily, their strength was ample yet they did not seek to show it off—they were horses for going far.
translations.idiomatic: They took much yet asked for little; their strength was deep yet they did not strain to show it. That is the stuff of distance-runners.

sentences.zh: 不幸相繼以死。

translations.literal: Unhappily they died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Both, alas, died in succession.

sentences.zh: 今所乘者，日不過數升，而秣不擇粟，飲不擇泉，攬轡未安，踊踴疾驅，甫百里，力竭汗喘，殆欲斃然。

translations.literal: The one I now ride eats no more than several sheng a day, yet in fodder does not choose grain, in drink does not choose spring; before the reins are settled it prances and rushes at speed; after barely a hundred li its strength is spent, it sweats and gasps, almost as if about to die.
translations.idiomatic: The horse I ride now eats only a few sheng a day, yet takes any grain and any water. Before the reins are even steady it is leaping and bolting. A hundred li and it is spent—sweating, gasping, nearly dead.

sentences.zh: 此其寡取易盈，好逞易窮，駑鈍之材也。

translations.literal: This is because it takes little yet is easily filled, loves to show off yet is easily exhausted—it is the stuff of dull nags.
translations.idiomatic: It asks little yet is easily satisfied; it loves to show off yet fails quickly. That is the stuff of nags.

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善，曰：「卿今議論極進。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised it and said, "Your discourse today has advanced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved and said, "Your thinking has grown sharper than ever."

sentences.zh: 」拜太尉，繼除宣撫使兼營田大使。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Grand Marshal, and then appointed Pacification Commissioner concurrently as Grand Commissioner of Military Colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Marshal and then pacification commissioner with concurrent charge of military colonies.

sentences.zh: 從幸建康，以王德、酈瓊兵隸飛，詔諭德等曰：「聽飛號令，如朕親行。」

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial progress to Jiankang, the troops of Wang De and Li Qiong were placed under Fei; an edict instructed De and the others, "Obey Fei's commands as if We were personally on campaign."
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial visit to Jiankang, the troops of Wang De and Li Qiong were placed under Yue Fei. An edict told them: "Obey Yue Fei's orders as if the emperor himself were in the field."

sentences.zh: 飛數見帝，論恢復之略。

translations.literal: Fei repeatedly saw the Emperor and discussed the strategy for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei saw the emperor again and again to discuss the strategy of recovery.

sentences.zh: 又手疏言：「金人所以立劉豫於河南，蓋欲荼毒中原，以中國攻中國，粘罕因得休兵觀釁。

translations.literal: He also wrote by hand, saying, "The reason the Jurchens set up Liu Yu in Henan is surely to poison the Central Plains, to use China to attack China, so that Nianhan can rest his troops and watch for openings.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote in his own hand: "The Jin set Liu Yu up in Henan to poison the Central Plains—to set Chinese against Chinese—while Nianhan rested his troops and watched for a chance."

sentences.zh: 臣欲陛下假臣月日，便則提兵趨京、洛，據河陽、陝府、潼關，以號召五路叛將。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to grant me days and months; then I will at once lead troops toward the capital and Luoyang, hold Heyang, Shan Prefecture, and Tong Pass, and summon the defecting generals of the five circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Give me time, and I will march on the capital and Luoyang, hold Heyang, Shanzhou, and Tong Pass, and call the defecting generals of the five circuits back to us.

sentences.zh: 叛將既還，遣王師前進，彼必棄汴而走河北，京畿、陝右可以盡復。

translations.literal: Once the defecting generals have returned, send the imperial army forward; they will surely abandon Bian and flee to Hebei, and the capital region and Shan Right can be fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Once those generals return, send the imperial army forward. The enemy will abandon Kaifeng and flee to Hebei. The capital region and western Shan can be fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 然後分兵濬、滑，經略兩河，如此則劉豫成擒，金人可滅，社稷長久之計，實在此舉。

translations.literal: Then divide troops at Jun and Hua and plan the two He regions; thus Liu Yu can be captured alive, the Jurchens can be destroyed—the long-term plan for the altars of state truly lies in this move.
translations.idiomatic: Then split forces at Junzhou and Huazhou and take the two He regions. Liu Yu will be taken alive, the Jin can be destroyed—the dynasty's lasting security rests on this one stroke.

sentences.zh: 」帝答曰：「有臣如此，顧復何憂，進止之機，朕不中制。

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied, "With a minister like this, what need we turn back to worry? As for the timing of advance and halt, We will not control from the center.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "With a minister like you, what have I to fear? When to advance and when to halt—I will not second-guess you from the palace."

sentences.zh: 」又召至寢閣命之曰：「中興之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: " He also summoned him to the sleeping quarters and commanded him, "The work of restoration—We entrust it entirely to you.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yue Fei to the private chamber and said, "The work of restoration—I leave it entirely to you."

sentences.zh: 」命節制光州。

translations.literal: " He was ordered to command Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was given command of Guangzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 飛方圖大舉，會秦檜主和，遂不以德、瓊兵隸飛。

translations.literal: Fei was just then planning a great offensive when Qin Hui advocated peace, and so De's and Qiong's troops were not placed under Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was planning a major offensive when Qin Hui took up the peace cause—and Wang De's and Li Qiong's troops were not placed under him.

sentences.zh: 詔詣都督府與張浚議事，浚謂飛曰：「王德淮西軍所服，浚欲以為都統，而命呂祉以督府參謀領之，如何？

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to go to the overall command headquarters to discuss affairs with Zhang Jun; Jun said to Fei, "Wang De is whom the Huai West army respects; Jun wishes to make him overall commander and order Lü Zhi as staff adviser of the headquarters to lead them—what say you?
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent him to the overall command to confer with Zhang Jun. Zhang Jun said, "Wang De is the man the Huai West army trusts. I want to make him overall commander and put Lü Zhi, a staff officer, over them. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「德與瓊素不相下，一旦揠之在上，則必爭。

translations.literal: " Fei said, "De and Qiong have never yielded to each other; once one is pulled up above, they will surely contend.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei said, "Wang De and Li Qiong have never accepted each other's rank. Put one over the other and they will fight."

sentences.zh: 呂尚書不習軍旅，恐不足服衆。

translations.literal: Minister Lü is not versed in military affairs; I fear he will not suffice to command the host.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lü knows nothing of war. I doubt he can command them.

sentences.zh: 」浚曰：「張宣撫如何？

translations.literal: " Jun said, "What of Pacification Commissioner Zhang?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jun said, "What about Commissioner Zhang?"

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「暴而寡謀，尤瓊所不服。

translations.literal: " Fei said, "He is violent and short on planning; Qiong especially will not submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei said, "He is brutal and rash. Li Qiong will never obey him."

sentences.zh: 」浚曰：「然則楊沂中爾？

translations.literal: " Jun said, "Then Yang Yizhong?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jun said, "Then Yang Yizhong?"

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「沂中視德等爾，豈能馭此軍？

translations.literal: " Fei said, "Yizhong is no better than De and the others—how could he control this army?
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei said, "Yizhong is no better than Wang De and the rest. How could he lead this army?"

sentences.zh: 」浚艴然曰：「浚固知非太尉不可。

translations.literal: " Jun flushed angrily and said, "Jun knew all along that none but the Grand Marshal would do.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jun flushed and said, "I knew all along only the Grand Marshal would do."

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「都督以正問飛，不敢不盡其愚，豈以得兵為念耶？

translations.literal: " Fei said, "The Commissioner asked Fei in earnest; I dare not fail to speak my full foolishness—how could I be thinking of gaining troops?
translations.idiomatic: " Yue Fei said, "You asked me honestly, Commissioner. I had to speak my mind. Do you think I was angling for more troops?"

sentences.zh: 」即日上章乞解兵柄，終喪服，以張憲攝軍事，步歸，廬母墓側。

translations.literal: " That same day he memorialized begging to relinquish military authority, completed mourning dress, had Zhang Xian act as military affairs, and walked home to lodge beside his mother's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he petitioned to surrender command, finished his mourning dress, left Zhang Xian in charge of the army, and walked home to keep vigil at his mother's grave.

sentences.zh: 浚怒，奏以張宗元為宣撫判官，監其軍。

translations.literal: Jun was angry and memorialized to appoint Zhang Zongyuan as Pacification Vice Commissioner to supervise his army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, furious, petitioned to appoint Zhang Zongyuan pacification vice commissioner to supervise the army.

sentences.zh: 帝累詔趣飛還職，飛力辭，詔幕屬造廬以死請，凡六日，飛趨朝待罪，帝慰遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly edicted urging Fei to return to office; Fei forcefully declined; an edict ordered staff members to build a lodge and beg with their lives; for six days in all Fei hurried to court to await punishment, and the Emperor comforted and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent edict after edict pressing Yue Fei to return. He refused. The court ordered his staff to build a lodge and beg him with their lives. After six days Yue Fei came to court to accept punishment. The emperor comforted him and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 宗元還言：「將和士銳，人懷忠孝，皆飛訓養所致。

translations.literal: Zongyuan returned and reported, "Generals are harmonious and soldiers keen; men cherish loyalty and filial piety—all this comes from Fei's training and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyuan reported back: "Officers live in harmony and the men are sharp; loyalty and devotion run through the ranks—all from Yue Fei's training."

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「比者寢閣之命，咸謂聖斷已堅，何至今尚未決？

translations.literal: Fei memorialized, "The recent command in the sleeping quarters—all said the sacred decision was already firm; why to this day has it still not been settled?
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei memorialized: "After your command in the private chamber, everyone believed the decision was firm. Why is nothing settled yet?"

sentences.zh: 臣願提兵進討，順天道，因人心，以曲直為老壯，以逆順為強弱，萬全之効可必。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to lead troops forward in punitive expedition, follow Heaven's way, rely on men's hearts, take right and wrong as old and young, take rebellion and compliance as strong and weak—an effect of complete security can be assured.
translations.idiomatic: Let me lead the army north. Follow Heaven's way and men's hearts; let right and wrong decide who stands firm, loyalty and treason decide who is strong. Victory will be certain.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「錢塘僻在海隅，非用武地。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized, "Qiantang lies remote at the sea's edge; it is not a place for employing arms.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Qiantang sits at the edge of the sea—it is no place to make war from."

sentences.zh: 願陛下建都上游，用漢光武故事，親率六軍，往來督戰。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to establish the capital in the upper reaches, following the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of Han, personally leading the Six Armies, going back and forth to supervise the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Move the capital upstream, as Emperor Guangwu of Han did. Lead the Six Armies yourself and ride back and forth to direct the fighting.

sentences.zh: 庶將士知聖意所向，人人用命。

translations.literal: Then perhaps the generals and soldiers will know where the sacred will points, and every man will give his life in service.
translations.idiomatic: Then every soldier will know where the throne stands, and every man will fight with his whole heart.

sentences.zh: 」未報而酈瓊叛，浚始悔。

translations.literal: " Before a reply came Li Qiong rebelled, and Jun began to regret.
translations.idiomatic: Before any answer came, Li Qiong rebelled—and Zhang Jun began to regret.

sentences.zh: 飛復奏：「願進屯淮甸，伺便擊瓊，期於破滅。

translations.literal: Fei again memorialized, "I wish to advance and encamp in the Huai region, watch for an opening to strike Qiong, and expect to break and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei petitioned again: "Let me advance to the Huai country, watch for a chance, and destroy Li Qiong."

sentences.zh: 」不許，詔駐師江州為淮、浙援。

translations.literal: " Permission was not granted; an edict ordered him to station troops at Jiang Prefecture as relief for Huai and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused and ordered him to hold Jiangzhou as support for the Huai and Zhe regions.

sentences.zh: 飛知劉豫結粘罕，而兀朮惡劉豫，可以間而動。

translations.literal: Fei knew Liu Yu was allied with Nianhan while Wuzhu hated Liu Yu, and that they could be set against each other and moved by discord.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei knew Liu Yu was tied to Nianhan while Wuzhu despised Liu Yu—a rift that could be exploited.

sentences.zh: 會軍中得兀朮諜者，飛陽責之曰：「汝非吾軍中人張斌耶？

translations.literal: Just then a spy of Wuzhu was captured in the army; Fei feigned rebuke, saying, "Are you not Zhang Bin of our army?
translations.idiomatic: A Wuzhu spy was captured in camp. Yue Fei feigned anger: "Aren't you Zhang Bin, one of our men?"

sentences.zh: 吾向遣汝至齊，約誘至四太子，汝往不復來。

translations.literal: I formerly sent you to Qi, with an agreement to lure the Fourth Prince here; you went and never returned.
translations.idiomatic: I sent you to Qi to lure the Fourth Prince here. You went and never came back.

sentences.zh: 吾繼遣人問，齊已許我，今冬以會合寇江為名，致四太子于清河。

translations.literal: I subsequently sent men to inquire; Qi had already agreed with us; this winter, under the pretext of joining forces to raid the river region, they would bring the Fourth Prince to Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: I sent men after that to follow up. Qi had already agreed: this winter, under cover of a joint raid on the south, they would bring the Fourth Prince to Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 汝所持書竟不至，何背我耶？

translations.literal: The letter you were to carry never arrived—why have you betrayed me?
translations.idiomatic: The letter you were supposed to deliver never came. Why have you turned against me?

sentences.zh: 」諜冀緩死，即詭服。

translations.literal: " The spy hoped to delay death and at once pretended submission.
translations.idiomatic: " The spy, hoping to save his life, feigned obedience at once.

sentences.zh: 乃作蠟書，言與劉豫同謀誅兀朮事，因謂諜曰：「吾今貸汝。

translations.literal: He then made a wax-sealed letter speaking of plotting with Liu Yu to kill Wuzhu, and said to the spy, "I spare you today.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a wax-sealed letter describing a plot with Liu Yu to kill Wuzhu, and told the spy, "I am letting you live.

sentences.zh: 」復遣至齊，問舉兵期，刲股納書，戒勿泄。

translations.literal: " He again sent him to Qi to inquire the date for raising troops, cut flesh from his thigh and hid the letter inside, and warned him not to reveal it.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent him back to Qi to ask when they would rise, cut flesh from his thigh to hide the letter inside, and forbade him to breathe a word.

sentences.zh: 諜歸，以書示兀朮，兀朮大驚，馳白其主，遂廢豫。

translations.literal: The spy returned and showed the letter to Wuzhu; Wuzhu was greatly alarmed, galloped to report to his lord, and Liu Yu was then deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The spy returned and showed the letter to Wuzhu. Wuzhu was shocked, raced to tell his sovereign, and Liu Yu was deposed.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「宜乘廢豫之際，擣其不備，長驅以取中原。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized, "We should seize the moment of Liu Yu's deposition, strike where they are unprepared, and drive deep to recover the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei memorialized: "We must strike while Liu Yu's removal has them off balance—drive hard and retake the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 八年，還軍鄂州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he returned the army to E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he brought the army back to Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 王庶視師江、淮，飛與庶書：「今歲若不舉兵，當納節請閑。

translations.literal: Wang Shu inspected the army on the Yangzi and Huai; Fei wrote to Shu, "If we do not raise troops this year, I should surrender my seal and request retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu was touring the Jiang and Huai fronts. Yue Fei wrote to him: "If we do not march this year, I will surrender my command and ask to retire."

sentences.zh: 」庶甚壯之。

translations.literal: " Shu greatly approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu admired the sentiment.

sentences.zh: 秋，召赴行在，命詣資善堂見皇太子。

translations.literal: In autumn he was summoned to the temporary capital and ordered to go to the Hall of Virtuous Learning to see the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was summoned to court and told to visit the crown prince in the Hall of Virtuous Learning.

sentences.zh: 飛退而喜曰：「社稷得人矣，中興基業，其在是乎？

translations.literal: Fei withdrew and said joyfully, "The altars of state have found their man; the foundation of restoration—surely it lies here?
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei left overjoyed: "The dynasty has found its heir. The work of restoration begins here—does it not?"

sentences.zh: 」會金遣使將歸河南地，飛言：「金人不可信，和好不可恃，相臣謀國不臧，恐貽後世譏」檜銜之。

translations.literal: " Just then the Jin sent envoys to return Henan territory; Fei said, "The Jurchens cannot be trusted, peace cannot be relied upon; the chief minister's planning for the state is unsound, and I fear it will bring mockery from later ages" Qin Hui bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Jin envoys arrived to return Henan. Yue Fei said, "The Jin are not to be trusted, peace is no foundation to stand on—the chief minister's counsel will invite the scorn of history." Qin Hui never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 九年，以復河南，大赦。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because Henan was recovered, a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year a general amnesty was proclaimed for the recovery of Henan.

sentences.zh: 飛表謝，寓和議不便之意，有「唾手燕雲，復讎報國」之語。

translations.literal: Fei submitted a memorial of thanks, conveying disapproval of the peace talks, with the words "with spit on our hands reach Yan and Yun, avenge and repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei submitted thanks but made his distrust of peace plain, writing that they could "reach Yan and Yun as easily as wiping one's hand—avenging the realm and repaying the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 授開府儀同三司，飛力辭，謂：「今日之事，可危而不可安；

translations.literal: He was granted Grand Master with the Same Ceremonials as the Three Councillors of State; Fei forcefully declined, saying, "Today's situation is one to fear, not to feel secure in;
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Grand Master with Ceremonials Equal to the Three Dukes. Yue Fei refused firmly: "The times call for dread, not complacency;

sentences.zh: 可憂而不可賀；

translations.literal: one to worry over, not to celebrate;
translations.idiomatic: for worry, not celebration;

sentences.zh: 可訓兵飭士，謹備不虞，而不可論功行賞，取笑敵人。

translations.literal: one in which to train troops and discipline soldiers, guard carefully against the unexpected, and not to discuss merit and dispense rewards, inviting the enemy's mockery.
translations.idiomatic: for drilling troops and staying alert—not for handing out honors that make us a laughingstock to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」三詔不受，帝溫言獎諭，乃受。

translations.literal: " Three edicts he did not accept; the Emperor spoke warmly in encouragement, and then he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he refused the edict. The emperor spoke warmly until at last he accepted.

sentences.zh: 會遣士㒟謁諸陵，飛請以輕騎從洒埽，實欲觀釁以伐謀。

translations.literal: Just then an envoy Shi Rui was sent to visit the imperial tombs; Fei requested to accompany with light cavalry for sweeping and cleaning, in truth wishing to watch for openings to plan an offensive.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy named Shi Rui was sent to tend the imperial tombs. Yue Fei asked to escort him with light cavalry—ostensibly to sweep the tombs, in truth to scout for a chance to strike.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「金人無事請和，此必有肘腋之虞，名以地歸我，實寄之也。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "The Jurchens seek peace without cause; there must be trouble at the flank and armpit; in name they return land to us, in reality they are lodging it with us.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The Jin offer peace for no reason. This hides trouble close at hand. They call it returning territory; in truth they are storing it with us."

sentences.zh: 」檜白帝止其行。

translations.literal: " Qin Hui told the Emperor to stop his journey.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui persuaded the emperor to forbid the trip.

sentences.zh: 十年，金人攻拱、亳，劉錡告急，命飛馳援，飛遣張憲、姚政赴之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Jurchens attacked Gong and Bo; Liu Qi reported urgency; Fei was ordered to rush to aid; Fei sent Zhang Xian and Yao Zheng to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Jin attacked Gongzhou and Bozhou. Liu Qi called for help. Yue Fei was ordered to hurry to his aid and sent Zhang Xian and Yao Zheng ahead.

sentences.zh: 帝賜札曰：「設施之方，一以委卿，朕不遙度。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed a letter saying, "As for methods of execution, We entrust all to you; We will not judge from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote: "How you carry this out I leave entirely to you. I will not second-guess you from the palace."

sentences.zh: 」飛乃遣王貴、牛皐、董先、楊再興、孟邦傑、李寶等，分布經略西京、汝、鄭、穎昌、陳、曹、光、蔡諸郡；

translations.literal: " Fei then sent Wang Gui, Niu Gao, Dong Xian, Yang Zaixing, Meng Bangjie, Li Bao, and others to distribute themselves and plan operations across the Western Capital, Ru, Zheng, Yingchang, Chen, Cao, Guang, and Cai prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sent Wang Gui, Niu Gao, Dong Xian, Yang Zaixing, Meng Bangjie, Li Bao, and others to take command across the Western Capital, Ruzhou, Zhengzhou, Yingchang, Chenzhou, Caozhou, Guangzhou, and Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 又命梁興渡河，糾合忠義社，取河東、北州縣。

translations.literal: He also ordered Liang Xing to cross the river, rally the Loyalty and Righteousness Societies, and take the prefectures and counties of Hedong and northern Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liang Xing to cross the river, rally the Loyalty and Righteousness societies, and recover Hedong and northern Hebei.

sentences.zh: 又遣兵東援劉錡，西援郭浩，自以其軍長驅以闞中原。

translations.literal: He also sent troops east to aid Liu Qi and west to aid Guo Hao, and personally led his army in a long drive to press into the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men east to Liu Qi and west to Guo Hao, then led his own army in a long thrust toward the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 將發，密奏言：「先正國本以安人心，然後不常厥居，以示無忘復讎之意。

translations.literal: About to set out, he secretly memorialized, "First establish the foundation of the state to settle men's hearts, then do not dwell in one place permanently, to show that the intent to avenge is not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Before marching he wrote in secret: "First settle the succession to calm the realm. Then do not keep a fixed capital—show that we have not forgotten revenge."

sentences.zh: 」帝得奏，大褒其忠，授少保，河南府路、陝西、河東北路招討使，尋改河南、北諸路招討使。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor received the memorial he greatly praised his loyalty, appointed him Junior Guardian, Pacification Commissioner of Henan Prefecture Circuit, Shaanxi, and Hedong North Circuit, and soon changed this to Pacification Commissioner of all Henan and northern circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and praised his devotion, made him Junior Guardian and pacification commissioner for Henan, Shaanxi, and northern Hedong—then pacification commissioner for all Henan and the northern circuits.

sentences.zh: 未幾，所遣諸將相繼奏捷。

translations.literal: Before long the generals he had sent reported victories one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his commanders began reporting victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 大軍在穎昌，諸將分道出戰，飛自以輕騎駐郾城，兵勢甚銳。

translations.literal: The main army was at Yingchang; the generals went out to fight by separate routes; Fei personally stationed himself at Yancheng with light cavalry, and the army's momentum was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The main force held Yingchang while his generals struck on every front. Yue Fei himself camped at Yancheng with light cavalry. His army's edge was razor-sharp.

sentences.zh: 兀朮大懼，會龍虎大王議，以為諸帥易與，獨飛不可當，欲誘致其師，併力一戰。

translations.literal: Wuzhu was greatly afraid; meeting with the Dragon-Tiger King to discuss, they judged the other commanders easy to deal with but Fei alone could not be withstood; they wished to lure his army forth and join forces for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu was terrified. He met with the Dragon-Tiger King and decided the Song commanders were easy prey except Yue Fei. They would lure Yue Fei's army out and crush it in one battle.

sentences.zh: 中外聞之，大懼，詔飛審處自固。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court, on hearing this, all were greatly afraid; an edict ordered Fei to judge the situation and secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country were alarmed. An edict told Yue Fei to weigh the situation and hold firm.

sentences.zh: 飛曰：「金人伎窮矣。

translations.literal: Fei said, "The Jurchens' tricks are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei said, "The Jin are at their wits' end."

sentences.zh: 」乃日出挑戰，且罵之。

translations.literal: " Then each day he went out to offer battle and cursed them.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he rode out to challenge them—and to curse them.

sentences.zh: 兀朮怒，合龍虎大王、蓋天大王與韓常之兵逼郾城。

translations.literal: Wuzhu grew angry, combined the forces of the Dragon-Tiger King, the Sky-Covering King, and Han Chang, and pressed on Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu, enraged, marched on Yancheng with the Dragon-Tiger King, the Sky-Covering King, and Han Chang.

sentences.zh: 飛遣子雲領騎兵直貫其陣，戒之曰：「不勝，先斬汝！

translations.literal: Fei sent his son Yun leading cavalry to pierce straight through their formation, warning him, "If you do not win, you will be beheaded first!
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sent his son Yue Yun at the head of the cavalry to drive through their lines, warning him: "Lose and I will take your head first!"

sentences.zh: 」鏖戰數十合，賊屍布野。

translations.literal: " After scores of fierce engagements, rebel corpses covered the field.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of savage clashes, enemy dead carpeted the field.

sentences.zh: 初，兀朮有勁軍，皆重鎧，貫以韋索，三人為聯，號「拐子馬」，官軍不能當。

translations.literal: Earlier Wuzhu had crack troops all in heavy armor, linked by leather ropes with three men in each chain, called "Linked Cavalry"; the government army could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu's crack troops wore heavy armor and were roped together three abreast—the "Linked Cavalry"—and the government troops could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 是役也，以萬五千騎來，飛戒步卒以麻札刀入陣，勿仰視，第斫馬足。

translations.literal: In this battle fifteen thousand horsemen came; Fei ordered the foot soldiers to enter the formation with hemp-braced sabers, not to look up, but only to chop at the horses' legs.
translations.idiomatic: This time fifteen thousand riders came. Yue Fei told his infantry to go in with maza sabers, eyes down, and cut at the horses' legs.

sentences.zh: 拐子馬相連，一馬仆，二馬不能行，官軍奮擊，遂大敗之。

translations.literal: The Linked Cavalry were chained together; when one horse fell, two could not move; the government army struck fiercely and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Roped together, when one horse fell the others could not move. The government troops charged and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 兀朮大慟曰：「自海上起兵，皆以此勝，今已矣！

translations.literal: Wuzhu wailed greatly, saying, "Since we raised arms at the sea, we have won by this—now it is over!
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu wept: "Since we took up arms on the coast we have won with these horses—now it is finished!"

sentences.zh: 」兀朮益兵來，部將王剛以五十騎覘敵，遇之，奮斬其將。

translations.literal: " Wuzhu brought more troops; the subordinate commander Wang Gang with fifty horsemen reconnoitered the enemy, met them, and fiercely beheaded their general.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu sent reinforcements. Wang Gang rode out with fifty men to scout, met the enemy, and cut down their commander.

sentences.zh: 飛時出視戰地，望見黃塵蔽天，自以四十騎突戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Fei was just then out surveying the battlefield; seeing yellow dust filling the sky, he personally took forty horsemen into a sudden attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was inspecting the field when he saw dust blot out the sky. He charged with forty riders and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 方郾城再捷，飛謂雲曰：「賊屢敗，必還攻穎昌，汝宜速援王貴。

translations.literal: Just as Yancheng had won twice, Fei said to Yun, "The bandits have been defeated repeatedly; they will surely turn to attack Yingchang; you should hurry to aid Wang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: After a second victory at Yancheng Yue Fei told Yue Yun: "The enemy keeps losing. They will hit Yingchang next. Go help Wang Gui at once."

sentences.zh: 」既而兀朮果至，貴將遊奕、雲將背嵬戰于城西。

translations.literal: " Soon Wuzhu indeed arrived; Gui commanded the Mobile Corps and Yun commanded the Beiyue troops fighting west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu came as predicted. Wang Gui led the Mobile Corps; Yue Yun led the Beiyue troops. They fought west of the city.

sentences.zh: 雲以騎兵八百挺前決戰，步軍張左右翼繼之，殺兀朮婿夏金吾、副統軍粘罕索孛堇，兀朮遁去。

translations.literal: Yun with eight hundred horsemen pressed forward for the decisive battle; infantry spread left and right wings to follow; they killed Wuzhu's son-in-law Xia Jinwu and vice-commander Nianhan Suo Boqin, and Wuzhu fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yun led eight hundred cavalry straight into the decisive fight; infantry opened both wings behind him. They killed Wuzhu's son-in-law Xia Jinwu and the vice-commander Nianhan Suo Boqin. Wuzhu fled.

sentences.zh: 梁興會太行忠義及兩河豪傑等，累戰皆捷，中原大震。

translations.literal: Liang Xing joined with the loyalists of the Taihang and the heroes of the two He regions; battle after battle was won; the Central Plains were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xing linked up with Taihang loyalists and heroes of the two He regions. Victory followed victory. The Central Plains shook.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「興等過河，人心願歸朝廷。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized, "When Xing and the others crossed the river, men's hearts wished to return to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei wrote: "When Liang Xing and his men crossed the river, everyone wanted to come back to the court."

sentences.zh: 金兵累敗，兀朮等皆令老少北去，正中興之機。

translations.literal: The Jin troops had been defeated repeatedly; Wuzhu and the others had all ordered old and young northward—it perfectly fit the moment for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin keep losing. Wuzhu is sending families north. This is our moment for restoration.

sentences.zh: 」飛進軍朱仙鎮，距汴京四十五里，與兀朮對壘而陣，遣驍將以背嵬騎五百奮擊，大破之，兀朮遁還汴京。

translations.literal: " Fei advanced to Zhuxian Town, forty-five li from Bianjing, set battle lines facing Wuzhu's camp, sent a fierce general with five hundred Beiyue horsemen in a fierce attack, routed them greatly, and Wuzhu fled back to Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei pushed to Zhuxian Town, forty-five li from Kaifeng, and drew up facing Wuzhu. Five hundred Beiyue cavalry under a crack commander smashed the Jin line. Wuzhu ran back to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 飛檄陵臺令行視諸陵，葺治之。

translations.literal: Fei issued an order to the director of imperial tombs to go inspect the tombs and repair them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei ordered the tomb warden to inspect the imperial graves and put them in order.

sentences.zh: 先是，紹興五年，飛遣梁興等布德意，招結兩河豪傑，山砦韋銓、孫謀等斂兵固堡，以待王師，李通、胡清、李寶、李興、張恩、孫琪等舉衆來歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fifth year of Shaoxing, Fei had sent Liang Xing and others to spread benevolent intent and win over heroes of the two He regions; Wei Quan and Sun Mou of the mountain forts gathered troops and fortified their bastions to await the imperial army; Li Tong, Hu Qing, Li Bao, Li Xing, Zhang En, Sun Qi, and others led their hosts to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: As early as Shaoxing year five Yue Fei had sent Liang Xing and others to spread goodwill and win over heroes north of the river. Wei Quan and Sun Mou in the mountain forts gathered men and held their strongpoints for the imperial army. Li Tong, Hu Qing, Li Bao, Li Xing, Zhang En, Sun Qi, and others brought their followers over.

sentences.zh: 金人動息，山川險要，一時皆得其實。

translations.literal: The Jurchens' movements and rest, the passes and defiles—all were for a time known in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: For a time they knew every Jin movement and every mountain pass.

sentences.zh: 盡磁、相、開德、澤、潞、晉、絳、汾、隰之境，皆期日興兵，與官軍會。

translations.literal: Throughout the regions of Ci, Xiang, Kaide, Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, Fen, and Xi, all set dates to raise troops and join the government army.
translations.idiomatic: From Cizhou through Xiangzhou, Kaide, Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, Fen, and Xi, every district set a day to rise and meet the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 其所揭旗以「岳」為號，父老百姓爭挽車牽牛，載糗糧以餽義軍，頂盆焚香迎候者，充滿道路。

translations.literal: The banners they raised took "Yue" as their device; fathers, elders, and common people vied to pull carts and lead oxen, carrying dried grain to supply the volunteer army; those who placed incense bowls on their heads to welcome and wait filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: They flew banners with the character Yue. Peasants vied to haul grain for the loyalists. The roads thronged with people carrying incense on their heads to welcome the army.

sentences.zh: 自燕以南，金號令不行，兀朮欲簽軍以抗飛，河北無一人從者。

translations.literal: South of Yan the Jin orders no longer ran; Wuzhu wished to draft troops to resist Fei, and not one man in Hebei would follow.
translations.idiomatic: South of Yan the Jin could no longer enforce their orders. Wuzhu tried to draft men to fight Yue Fei—not one person in Hebei obeyed.

sentences.zh: 乃嘆曰：「自我起北方以來，未有如今日之挫衂。

translations.literal: He sighed and said, "Since I rose in the north, there has never been a setback like today's.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed: "Since I came out of the north I have never known a rout like this."

sentences.zh: 」金帥烏陵思謀素號桀黠，亦不能制其下，但諭之曰：「毋輕動，俟岳家軍來即降。

translations.literal: " The Jin commander Wulingsimou, known for fierce cunning, could not control his subordinates either, and could only instruct them, "Do not move rashly; when Yue's army comes, then surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Even Wulingsimou, the Jin commander famed for his ruthlessness, could not control his troops. He could only tell them: "Stay put. When Yue's army comes, surrender."

sentences.zh: 」金統制王鎮、統領崔慶、將官李覬崔虎華旺等皆率所部降，以至禁衞龍虎大王下忔查千戶高勇之屬，皆密受飛旗牓，自北方來降。

translations.literal: " The Jin controller Wang Zhen, commander Cui Qing, officers Li Yi, Cui Hu, Hua Wang, and others all led their units to surrender; down to the Palace Guard Dragon-Tiger King's subordinate Qianhu Gao Yong and the like—all had secretly received Fei's banners and placards and came to surrender from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Jin officers Wang Zhen, Cui Qing, Li Yi, Cui Hu, Hua Wang, and others brought their units over—even men under the Palace Guard Dragon-Tiger King such as Qianhu Gao Yong had secretly accepted Yue Fei's banners and defected from the north.

sentences.zh: 金將軍韓常欲以五萬衆內附。

translations.literal: The Jin general Han Chang wished to come over with fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Han Chang wanted to defect with fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 飛大喜，語其下曰：「直抵黃龍府，與諸君痛飲爾！」

translations.literal: Fei was greatly pleased and said to his men, "We will drive straight to Huanglong Prefecture and drink deep with you all!"
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei rejoiced and told his men: "We will march to Huanglong Prefecture and drink ourselves merry!"

sentences.zh: 方指日渡河，而檜欲畫淮以北棄之，風臺臣請班師。

translations.literal: Just as a date was set to cross the river, Qin Hui wished to draw a line and abandon everything north of the Huai; he prompted court officials to request withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: With a crossing day in sight, Qin Hui wanted to abandon everything north of the Huai and swayed officials to ask for withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 飛奏：「金人銳氣沮喪，盡棄輜重，疾走渡河，豪傑向風，士卒用命，時不再來，機難輕失。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized, "The Jurchens' sharp spirit is crushed and dejected; they have cast off all baggage and are fleeing hastily across the river; heroes turn their faces to the wind, soldiers give their lives—time does not come twice, opportunity is not lightly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei petitioned: "The Jin are broken in spirit. They have dumped their baggage and are rushing north. Heroes are turning to us. The men will fight to the death. This moment will not return."

sentences.zh: 」檜知飛志銳不可回，乃先請張俊、楊沂中等歸，而後言飛孤軍不可久留，乞令班師。

translations.literal: " Qin Hui knew Fei's resolve was sharp and could not be turned back; he first asked Zhang Jun and Yang Yizhong and others to return, and then said Fei's isolated army could not long remain, begging that he be ordered to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui saw Yue Fei's resolve could not be bent. He first recalled Zhang Jun and Yang Yizhong, then argued that Yue Fei's lone army could not stay—and begged for withdrawal orders.

sentences.zh: 一日奉十二金字牌，飛憤惋泣下，東向再拜曰：「十年之力，廢於一旦。

translations.literal: One day he received twelve gold-lettered plaques; Fei wept in anger and grief, bowed twice toward the east, and said, "Ten years of effort wasted in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: One day twelve gold-letter plaques arrived. Yue Fei wept with rage, bowed twice to the east, and said: "Ten years of effort—ruined in a single day."

sentences.zh: 」飛班師，民遮馬慟哭，訴曰：「我等戴香盆、運糧草以迎官軍，金人悉知之。

translations.literal: " Fei withdrew his army; the people blocked his horse and wailed, pleading, "We wore incense basins on our heads and hauled grain to welcome the government army—the Jurchens know all of this.
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew, people blocked his horse and wept: "We welcomed you with incense and grain. The Jin know everything."

sentences.zh: 相公去，我輩無噍類矣。

translations.literal: When the lord goes, we will have no one left alive.
translations.idiomatic: When you leave, none of us will survive.

sentences.zh: 」飛亦悲泣，取詔示之曰：「吾不得擅留。

translations.literal: " Fei also wept in grief, took out the edict to show them, and said, "I may not stay without authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei wept too. He showed them the edict: "I cannot stay without orders."

sentences.zh: 」哭聲震野，飛留五日以待其徙，從而南者如市，亟奏以漢上六郡閒田處之。

translations.literal: " Wailing shook the countryside; Fei stayed five days to wait for their migration; those who followed south were like a market crowd; he urgently memorialized to settle them on idle lands in the six Han River prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wailing filled the fields. Yue Fei waited five days for refugees to move. The stream of people heading south was endless. He urgently petitioned to resettle them on idle lands in the six Han River prefectures.

sentences.zh: 方兀朮棄汴去，有書生叩馬曰：「太子毋走，岳少保且退矣。

translations.literal: Just as Wuzhu was abandoning Bian and leaving, a scholar knocked on his horse and said, "Prince, do not flee—Lord Yue the Junior Guardian is about to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: As Wuzhu was leaving Kaifeng a scholar stopped his horse: "Prince, do not go—Lord Yue is about to pull back."

sentences.zh: 」兀朮曰：「岳少保以五百騎破吾十萬，京城日夜望其來，何謂可守？

translations.literal: " Wuzhu said, "Lord Yue with five hundred horsemen broke my hundred thousand—the capital day and night waits for his coming; how do you say it can be held?
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu said, "Lord Yue broke a hundred thousand of us with five hundred riders. The capital has been praying for him day and night. How can we hold it?"

sentences.zh: 」生曰：「自古未有權臣在內，而大將能立功於外者，岳少保且不免，況欲成功乎？

translations.literal: " The scholar said, "Since antiquity there has never been a powerful minister within while a great general could achieve merit outside—Lord Yue cannot even escape harm, how much less succeed?
translations.idiomatic: The scholar said, "Never in history has a great general won glory abroad while a powerful minister ruled at court. Lord Yue will not even save himself—how could he finish the job?"

sentences.zh: 」兀朮悟，遂留。

translations.literal: " Wuzhu understood and stayed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu understood—and stayed.

sentences.zh: 飛既歸，所得州縣，旋復失之。

translations.literal: After Fei returned, the prefectures and counties he had taken were soon lost again.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue Fei withdrew, every county and prefecture he had taken was lost again.

sentences.zh: 飛力請解兵柄，不許，自廬入觀，帝問之，飛拜謝而已。

translations.literal: Fei forcefully begged to relinquish military authority; permission was not granted; coming from Lu to audience, when the Emperor asked him, Fei only bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei begged to give up command; the court refused. He came from Lushan to court. When the emperor asked him questions, he only bowed and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，諜報金分道渡淮，飛請合諸帥之兵破敵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, spies reported the Jurchens crossing the Huai by separate routes; Fei requested to unite the great commanders' armies to break the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year spies reported the Jin crossing the Huai on several fronts. Yue Fei asked to combine the commanders' forces and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 兀朮、韓常與龍虎大王疾驅至廬，帝趣飛應援，凡十七札。

translations.literal: Wuzhu, Han Chang, and the Dragon-Tiger King galloped fast to Lu; the Emperor urged Fei to go to aid; altogether seventeen letters.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu, Han Chang, and the Dragon-Tiger King raced on Luzhou. The emperor sent Yue Fei seventeen urgent messages to go to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 飛策金人舉國南來，巢穴必虛，若長驅京、洛以擣之，彼必奔命，可坐而敝。

translations.literal: Fei judged that with the Jurchens coming south with their entire nation, their nest would surely be empty; if one drove long to the capital and Luoyang to strike them, they would surely run to save themselves, and one could sit and wear them out.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei reasoned that if the whole Jin host was marching south, their base must be empty. A long strike at Kaifeng and Luoyang would force them to hurry back—we could wear them down without a fight.

sentences.zh: 時飛方苦寒嗽，力疾而行。

translations.literal: At that time Fei was just then suffering cold and a bad cough; he forced himself onward despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was racked with a cold cough but forced himself onward.

sentences.zh: 又恐帝急於退敵，乃奏：「臣如擣虛，勢必得利，若以為敵方在近，未暇遠圖，欲乞親至蘄、黃，以議攻卻。

translations.literal: Fearing the Emperor was eager to repel the enemy quickly, he memorialized, "If your subject strikes the empty nest, we are sure to gain; if you think the enemy is near and there is no leisure for distant planning, I beg to go in person to Qi and Huang to discuss attack and repulse.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor wanted a quick repulse, he wrote: "If I strike their empty base we will win—but if Your Majesty thinks the enemy is too close for a distant campaign, let me go in person to Qizhou and Huangzhou to plan the counterattack."

sentences.zh: 」帝得奏大喜，賜札曰：「卿苦寒疾，乃為朕行，國爾忘身，誰如卿者？

translations.literal: " When the Emperor received the memorial he was greatly pleased and bestowed a letter saying, "You suffer cold illness yet go for Us—forgetting self for the state—who is like you?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it with joy and wrote back: "You are ill with cold yet you march for me—you forget yourself for the realm. Who is like you?"

sentences.zh: 」師至廬州，金兵望風而遁。

translations.literal: " When the army reached Luz Prefecture, the Jurchen troops fled at sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: When his army reached Luzhou the Jin fled at the mere rumor of his approach.

sentences.zh: 飛還兵于舒以俟命，帝又賜札，以飛小心恭謹、不專進退為得體。

translations.literal: Fei returned the army to Shu to await orders; the Emperor again bestowed a letter, praising Fei's careful reverence and not presuming over advance and withdrawal as proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei held his troops at Shuzhou awaiting orders. The emperor wrote again, praising his caution and restraint in not taking advance or withdrawal into his own hands.

sentences.zh: 兀朮破濠州，張俊駐軍黃連鎮，不敢進；

translations.literal: Wuzhu broke Hao Prefecture; Zhang Jun encamped his army at Huanglian Town and did not dare advance;
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu took Haozhou. Zhang Jun camped at Huanglian Town and would not advance;

sentences.zh: 楊沂中遇伏而敗，帝命飛救之。

translations.literal: Yang Yizhong met an ambush and was defeated; the Emperor ordered Fei to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yizhong walked into an ambush and lost. The emperor ordered Yue Fei to save him.

sentences.zh: 金人聞飛至，又遁。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens heard Fei had arrived, they fled again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin heard Yue Fei was coming, they fled again.

sentences.zh: 時和議既決，檜患飛異己，乃密奏召三大將論功行賞。

translations.literal: At that time the peace agreement was already settled; Qin Hui feared Fei differed from him and secretly memorialized to summon the three great generals to discuss merit and dispense rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was settled. Qin Hui, fearing Yue Fei's independence, secretly petitioned to summon the three great commanders to discuss honors.

sentences.zh: 韓世忠、張俊已至，飛獨後，檜又用參政王次翁計，俟之六七日。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun had already arrived; Fei alone came late; Qin Hui again used Vice Grand Councillor Wang Ciweng's plan to make him wait six or seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun arrived first. Yue Fei came late—Qin Hui, following Vice Grand Councillor Wang Ciweng's advice, kept him waiting six or seven days.

sentences.zh: 既至，授樞密副使，位參知政事上，飛固請還兵柄。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, ranking above Vice Grand Councillor; Fei firmly begged to return military authority.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally arrived they made him Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, senior to the vice grand councillors. Yue Fei insisted on giving up his command.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔同俊往楚州措置邊防，總韓世忠軍還駐鎮江。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict ordered him together with Jun to go to Chu Prefecture to arrange border defenses; Han Shizhong's army was recalled to encamp at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he and Zhang Jun were ordered to Chu Prefecture to manage the frontier. Han Shizhong's army was recalled to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 初，飛在諸將中年最少，以列校拔起，累立顯功，世忠、俊不能平，飛屈己下之，幕中輕銳教飛勿苦降意。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the generals Fei was youngest; raised from rank-and-file officer, he repeatedly achieved great merit; Shizhong and Jun could not be reconciled to it; Fei humbled himself below them; the sharp young men on his staff urged Fei not to bother lowering himself so much.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was the youngest of the great generals, risen from the ranks. His victories unnerved Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun. He humbled himself before them, but his staff's hotheads told him not to demean himself so.

sentences.zh: 金人攻淮西，俊分地也，俊始不敢行，師卒無功。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked Huai West, it was Jun's assigned territory; Jun at first did not dare go; the army in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Huai West—Zhang Jun's sector—Zhang Jun dared not march. His army accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 飛聞命即行，遂解廬州圍，帝授飛兩鎮節，俊益恥。

translations.literal: Fei, on hearing the order, set out at once, relieved the siege of Lu Prefecture, and the Emperor granted Fei two military commissions; Jun grew all the more ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei marched the moment he was called, lifted the siege of Luzhou, and was given two military commissions—to Zhang Jun's further shame.

sentences.zh: 楊么平，飛獻俊、世忠樓船各一，兵械畢備，世忠大悅，俊反忌之。

translations.literal: When Yang Yao was pacified, Fei presented Jun and Shizhong each with a tower ship, weapons and gear fully complete; Shizhong was greatly pleased, Jun instead grew jealous.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yao's defeat Yue Fei gave Han Shizhong and Zhang Jun each a tower ship, fully equipped. Han Shizhong was delighted; Zhang Jun resented it.

sentences.zh: 淮西之役，俊以前途糧乏訹飛，飛不為止，帝賜札褒諭，有曰：「轉餉艱阻，卿不復顧。

translations.literal: In the Huai West campaign Jun intimidated Fei with warnings that grain ahead was scarce; Fei did not stop; the Emperor bestowed a letter of praise, saying, "Transport of provisions was difficult and obstructed, yet you did not look back.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huai West campaign Zhang Jun tried to scare Yue Fei off by warning of scarce supplies. Yue Fei pressed on. The emperor praised him: "Supply lines were choked—you did not waver."

sentences.zh: 」俊疑飛漏言，還朝，反倡言飛逗遛不進，以乏餉為辭。

translations.literal: " Jun suspected Fei had leaked his words; returning to court, he instead spread the claim that Fei lingered and would not advance, using lack of provisions as his excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun suspected Yue Fei had repeated his warnings. Back at court he accused Yue Fei of dawdling and using lack of supplies as an excuse.

sentences.zh: 至視世忠軍，俊知世忠忤檜，欲與飛分其背嵬軍，飛議不肯，俊大不悅。

translations.literal: When it came to inspecting Shizhong's army, Jun knew Shizhong had crossed Qin Hui and wished to divide his Beiyue troops with Fei; Fei in council refused, and Jun was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When they inspected Han Shizhong's troops Zhang Jun—knowing Han Shizhong had crossed Qin Hui—wanted Yue Fei to help him split up the Beiyue force. Yue Fei refused. Zhang Jun was furious.

sentences.zh: 及同行楚州城，俊欲修城為備，飛曰：「當戮力以圖恢復，豈可為退保計？

translations.literal: When they together went to Chu Prefecture city, Jun wished to repair the walls for defense; Fei said, "We should join strength to plan recovery—how can we make plans for retreat and self-preservation?
translations.idiomatic: Touring Chuzhou together Zhang Jun wanted to fortify the walls. Yue Fei said: "We should fight together for recovery—how can we plan only to fall back?"

sentences.zh: 」俊變色。

translations.literal: " Jun's face changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun's face darkened.

sentences.zh: 會世忠軍吏景著與總領胡紡言：「二樞密若分世忠軍，恐至生事。

translations.literal: Just then Han Shizhong's army clerk Jing Zhu spoke to the chief administrator Hu Fang, saying, "If the two commissioners of military affairs divide Shizhong's army, I fear trouble will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Han Shizhong's army clerk Jing Zhu told the chief administrator Hu Fang: "If the two commissioners of military affairs split up Han Shizhong's army, there will be trouble."

sentences.zh: 」紡上之朝，檜捕著下大理寺，將以扇搖誣世忠。

translations.literal: " Fang reported this to court; Qin Hui arrested Zhu and sent him to the Court of Judicial Review, intending to use him to incite and slander Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fang reported this to court. Qin Hui arrested Jing Zhu and sent him to the Court of Judicial Review, planning to use the case to undermine Han Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 飛馳書告以檜意，世忠見帝自明。

translations.literal: Fei sent an urgent letter revealing Qin Hui's intent; Shizhong went before the Emperor and cleared himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sent an urgent letter warning Han Shizhong of Qin Hui's scheme. Han Shizhong went to the emperor and cleared himself.

sentences.zh: 俊於是大憾飛，遂倡言飛議棄山陽，且密以飛報世忠事告檜，檜大怒。

translations.literal: Jun then deeply resented Fei; he spread word that Fei had proposed abandoning Shanyang, and secretly reported to Qin Hui about Fei's warning to Shizhong; Qin Hui was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun now hated Yue Fei with a passion. He spread rumors that Yue Fei wanted to abandon Shanyang, and secretly told Qin Hui about Yue Fei's warning to Han Shizhong. Qin Hui flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 初，檜逐趙鼎，飛每對客嘆息，又以恢復為己任，不肯附和議。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qin Hui drove out Zhao Ding, Fei would sigh whenever guests were present; he also took recovery of lost territory as his own duty and refused to go along with the peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui had driven Zhao Ding from office, Yue Fei would sigh in the company of guests. He made recovery of the north his personal mission and would not countenance peace.

sentences.zh: 讀檜奏，至「德無常師，主善為師」之語，惡其欺罔，恚曰：「君臣大倫，根於天性，大臣而忍面謾其主耶！

translations.literal: Reading Qin Hui's memorial, when he came to the words "virtue has no fixed teacher; the ruler who excels in virtue becomes the teacher," he detested the deception and said in anger, "The great bond between ruler and minister is rooted in nature—how can a great minister bear to lie to his lord's face!
translations.idiomatic: Reading one of Qin Hui's memorials, he came to the line "virtue has no fixed teacher; the ruler who excels in virtue becomes the teacher." Disgusted by the deceit, he fumed: "The bond between ruler and minister is rooted in nature—how can a great minister lie to his sovereign's face!"

sentences.zh: 」兀朮遺檜書曰：「汝朝夕以和請，而岳飛方為河北圖，必殺飛，始可和。

translations.literal: " Wuzhu sent Qin Hui a letter saying, "You plead for peace day and night, yet Yue Fei is just then plotting for Hebei—you must kill Fei before peace can be made.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu wrote to Qin Hui: "You plead for peace day and night, but Yue Fei is scheming to recover Hebei. Yue Fei must die before there can be peace."

sentences.zh: 」檜亦以飛不死，終梗和議，己必及禍，故力謀殺之。

translations.literal: " Qin Hui also believed that as long as Fei lived, the peace talks would ultimately be blocked and he himself would come to harm; therefore he strove to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui knew that as long as Yue Fei lived, peace would never hold and he himself would pay the price. He set out to kill him.

sentences.zh: 以諫議大夫万俟禼與飛有怨，風禼劾飛，又風中丞何鑄、侍御史羅汝楫交章彈論，大率謂：「今春金人攻淮西，飛略至舒、蘄而不進，比與俊按兵淮上，又欲棄山陽而不守。

translations.literal: Because Remonstrance and Policy Advisor Wan Qixie bore a grudge against Fei, he prompted Qixie to impeach Fei; he also prompted Vice Censor-in-Chief He Zhu and Attending Censor Luo Ruji to submit memorials in succession, generally saying, "This spring when the Jurchens attacked Huai West, Fei only reached Shu and Qi and did not advance; when he and Jun held their armies on the Huai, he also wished to abandon Shanyang and not defend it.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted Remonstrance and Policy Advisor Wan Qixie, who already hated Yue Fei, to impeach him, and prompted Vice Censor-in-Chief He Zhu and Attending Censor Luo Ruji to pile on. Their charge, in essence: "This spring when the Jin attacked Huai West, Yue Fei only reached Shuzhou and Qizhou and stopped. With Zhang Jun he held the Huai line but wanted to abandon Shanyang."

sentences.zh: 」飛累章請罷樞柄，尋還兩鎮節，充萬壽觀使、奉朝請。

translations.literal: " Fei repeatedly memorialized asking to relinquish his post at the Bureau of Military Affairs; soon his two military commissions were returned, and he was made Commissioner of the Wanshou View and a Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei repeatedly asked to give up his post at the Bureau of Military Affairs. His two military commissions were restored, and he was made Commissioner of the Wanshou View with the rank of Court Attendant.

sentences.zh: 檜志未伸也，又諭張俊令劫王貴、誘王俊誣告張憲謀還飛兵。

translations.literal: Qin Hui's aim was not yet fulfilled; he further instructed Zhang Jun to coerce Wang Gui and entice Wang Jun to falsely accuse Zhang Xian of plotting to restore Fei's army.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui's purpose was not yet served. He told Zhang Jun to coerce Wang Gui and entice Wang Jun into falsely accusing Zhang Xian of plotting to bring Yue Fei's army back.

sentences.zh: 檜遣使捕飛父子證張憲事，使者至，飛笑曰：「皇天后土，可表此心。

translations.literal: Qin Hui sent envoys to arrest Fei and his son to testify in the Zhang Xian case; when the envoys arrived, Fei laughed and said, "Heaven above and earth below can bear witness to this heart.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui sent men to arrest Yue Fei and his son as witnesses in the Zhang Xian case. When they arrived Yue Fei laughed and said: "Heaven and earth can bear witness to my heart."

sentences.zh: 」初命何鑄鞠之，飛裂裳以背示鑄，有「盡忠報國」四大字，深入膚理。

translations.literal: " At first He Zhu was ordered to interrogate him; Fei tore his garment and showed Zhu his back, where the four characters "Serve the State with Utmost Loyalty" were cut deep into the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhu was first assigned to interrogate him. Yue Fei tore open his robe and showed He Zhu his back, where the four characters "Serve the State with Utmost Loyalty" had been tattooed deep into the skin.

sentences.zh: 既而閱實無左驗，鑄明其無辜。

translations.literal: After investigation there was no corroborating evidence; Zhu declared him innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation found no corroborating evidence. He Zhu declared him innocent.

sentences.zh: 改命万俟禼。

translations.literal: The case was reassigned to Wan Qixie.
translations.idiomatic: The case was reassigned to Wan Qixie.

sentences.zh: 禼誣：飛與憲書，令虛申探報以動朝廷，雲與憲書，令措置使飛還軍；

translations.literal: Qixie fabricated charges: that Fei wrote to Xian ordering him to submit false intelligence reports to stir the court, and that Yun wrote to Xian ordering arrangements to bring Fei's army back;
translations.idiomatic: Wan Qixie fabricated charges: that Yue Fei had written Zhang Xian ordering false intelligence reports to stir the court, and that Yue Yun had written Zhang Xian to arrange Yue Fei's return to command;

sentences.zh: 且言其書已焚。

translations.literal: and claimed the letters had already been burned.
translations.idiomatic: and claimed the letters had already been burned.

sentences.zh: 飛坐繫兩月，無可證者。

translations.literal: Fei sat imprisoned for two months, and nothing could be proved.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sat in prison for two months. Nothing could be proved.

sentences.zh: 或教禼以臺章所指淮西事為言，禼喜白檜，簿錄飛家，取當時御札藏之以滅迹。

translations.literal: Someone advised Qixie to use the censorial memorials' charges about the Huai West affair as grounds; Qixie gladly reported this to Qin Hui, inventoried Fei's household, and took the imperial letters of the time and hid them to erase the trail.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Wan Qixie to build the case on the censorial charges about Huai West. Wan Qixie gladly told Qin Hui, inventoried Yue Fei's household, and seized the imperial letters of the time and hid them to destroy the evidence.

sentences.zh: 又逼孫革等證飛受詔逗遛，命評事元龜年取行軍時日雜定之，傅會其獄。

translations.literal: He also coerced Sun Ge and others to testify that Fei had received orders yet lingered; he ordered Reviewer Yuan Guinian to take marching dates and jumble them together, forcing the case to fit.
translations.idiomatic: He coerced Sun Ge and others into testifying that Yue Fei had dawdled despite orders, and had Reviewer Yuan Guinian jumble marching dates together to make the charges stick.

sentences.zh: 歲暮，獄不成，檜手書小紙付獄，即報飛死，時年三十九。

translations.literal: At year's end the case still would not stand; Qin Hui wrote a note by hand and sent it to the prison, and Fei's death was immediately reported—he was thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end the case still would not hold. Qin Hui wrote a note by hand and sent it to the prison. Yue Fei was reported dead. He was thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 雲棄市。

translations.literal: Yun was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yun was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 籍家貲，徙家嶺南。

translations.literal: The family's property was confiscated and the family was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The family's property was confiscated and the family was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 幕屬于鵬等從坐者六人。

translations.literal: Six staff members including Yu Peng were punished as accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Six members of his staff, including Yu Peng, were punished as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 初，飛在獄，大理寺丞李若樸何彥猷、大理卿薛仁輔並言飛無罪，禼俱劾去。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Fei was in prison, Court of Judicial Review Aide Li Ruopu and He Yanyou and Chief Minister of Justice Xue Renfu all said Fei was innocent; Qixie impeached them all and they were removed.
translations.idiomatic: While Yue Fei was in prison, Court of Judicial Review aides Li Ruopu and He Yanyou and Chief Minister of Justice Xue Renfu all declared him innocent. Wan Qixie impeached them all and they were removed.

sentences.zh: 宗正卿士㒟請以百口保飛，禼亦劾之，竄死建州。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Shi Rui asked to guarantee Fei with the lives of a hundred family members; Qixie impeached him too, and he was exiled and died in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan Shi Rui offered to guarantee Yue Fei with the lives of a hundred family members. Wan Qixie impeached him too. He was exiled and died in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 布衣劉允升上書訟飛冤，下棘寺以死。

translations.literal: Commoner Liu Yunsheng submitted a memorial pleading Fei's injustice; he was sent to the prison and died there.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Liu Yunsheng submitted a memorial pleading Yue Fei's innocence. He was sent to prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 凡傅成其獄者，皆遷轉有差。

translations.literal: All who helped fabricate the case received promotions of varying degree.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who helped fabricate the case was promoted.

sentences.zh: 獄之將上也，韓世忠不平，詣檜詰其實，檜曰：「飛子雲與張憲書雖不明，其事體莫須有。

translations.literal: When the case was about to be submitted, Han Shizhong was indignant; he went to Qin Hui to demand the truth, and Qin Hui said, "Though the letters between Fei's son Yun and Zhang Xian are unclear, the substance of the matter perhaps exists.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was about to go up, Han Shizhong was furious. He confronted Qin Hui and demanded the truth. Qin Hui said: "The letters between Yue Yun and Zhang Xian may be unclear, but the substance of the matter perhaps exists."

sentences.zh: 」世忠曰：「『莫須有』三字，何以服天下？

translations.literal: " Shizhong said, "The three words 'perhaps it exists'—how can they convince the world?
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong said: "'Perhaps it exists'—how can three words like that convince the world?"

sentences.zh: 」時洪皓在金國中，蠟書馳奏，以為金人所畏服者惟飛，至以父呼之，諸酋聞其死，酌酒相賀。

translations.literal: " At that time Hong Hao was in the Jin state; he sent a wax-sealed letter in haste to report that the Jurchens feared and respected none but Fei—they even called him "Father"—and when the chieftains heard of his death, they drank wine and congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Hao was then in Jin territory. He sent a wax-sealed dispatch reporting that the Jin feared no one but Yue Fei—they even called him "Father." When the chieftains heard of his death they drank wine and congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 飛至孝，母留河北，遣人求訪，迎歸。

translations.literal: Fei was deeply filial; his mother had remained in Hebei; he sent men to search for her and brought her back.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was deeply filial. His mother had remained in Hebei. He sent men to find her and brought her home.

sentences.zh: 母有痼疾，藥餌必親。

translations.literal: His mother had a chronic illness; he always administered her medicine in person.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had a chronic illness. He always prepared her medicine himself.

sentences.zh: 母卒，水漿不入口者三日。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he took neither water nor food for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he took neither food nor water for three days.

sentences.zh: 家無姬侍。

translations.literal: His household had no concubines or attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His household had no concubines.

sentences.zh: 吳玠素服飛，願與交驩，飾名姝遺之。

translations.literal: Wu Jie had long admired Fei and wished to become close friends; he sent him a famous beauty as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie had long admired Yue Fei and wished to befriend him. He sent him a famous beauty as a gift.

sentences.zh: 飛曰：「主上宵旰，豈大將安樂時？

translations.literal: Fei said, "The sovereign toils day and night—how can this be a time for a great general's ease and pleasure?
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei said: "The emperor toils day and night—how can a great general take his ease?"

sentences.zh: 」卻不受，玠益敬服。

translations.literal: " He refused the gift; Jie respected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He refused. Wu Jie respected him all the more.

sentences.zh: 少豪飲，帝戒之曰：「卿異時到河朔，乃可飲。

translations.literal: In youth he drank freely; the Emperor admonished him, saying, "When you reach Hebei and Shuo one day, then you may drink.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he drank freely. The emperor admonished him: "When you reach Hebei, then you may drink."

sentences.zh: 」遂絕不飲。

translations.literal: " From then on he stopped drinking entirely.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he never drank again.

sentences.zh: 帝初為飛營第，飛辭曰：「敵未滅，何以家為？

translations.literal: When the Emperor first built a mansion for Fei, Fei declined, saying, "The enemy is not yet destroyed—how can I think of home?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first built a mansion for him, Yue Fei declined: "The enemy is not yet destroyed—how can I think of home?"

sentences.zh: 」或問天下何時太平，飛曰：「文臣不愛錢，武臣不惜死，天下太平矣。」

translations.literal: " When someone asked when the realm would be at peace, Fei said, "When civil officials do not love money and military officers do not fear death, the realm will be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked when the realm would know peace, Yue Fei said: "When civil officials do not love money and military officers do not fear death, the realm will be at peace."

sentences.zh: 師每休捨，課將士注坡跳壕，皆重鎧習之。

translations.literal: Whenever the army rested in camp, he drilled the officers and soldiers in running slopes and leaping ditches, all in heavy armor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the army rested, he drilled his officers and men in running slopes and leaping ditches—all in heavy armor.

sentences.zh: 子雲嘗習注坡，馬躓，怒而鞭之。

translations.literal: His son Yun once practiced slope-running; his horse stumbled, and Fei angrily whipped him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue Yun once practiced slope-running. His horse stumbled and Yue Fei whipped him in anger.

sentences.zh: 卒有取民麻一縷以束芻者，立斬以徇。

translations.literal: A soldier who took a single strand of hemp from a civilian to bind fodder was immediately beheaded as an example.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier who took a single strand of hemp from a civilian to bind fodder was beheaded on the spot as an example.

sentences.zh: 卒夜宿，民開門願納，無敢入者。

translations.literal: When soldiers camped for the night, civilians opened their doors and wished to take them in, but none dared enter.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers camped overnight, civilians opened their doors to offer shelter—but none dared enter.

sentences.zh: 軍號「凍死不拆屋，餓死不鹵掠。

translations.literal: The army's motto was, "Better to freeze than tear down a house; better to starve than plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The army's motto was: "Better to freeze than tear down a house; better to starve than plunder."

sentences.zh: 」卒有疾，躬為調藥；

translations.literal: " When a soldier fell ill, he personally prepared his medicine;
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier fell ill, he prepared the medicine himself;

sentences.zh: 諸將遠戍，遣妻問勞其家；

translations.literal: when generals were stationed far away, he sent his wife to inquire after their families;
translations.idiomatic: when generals were stationed far away, he sent his wife to visit their families;

sentences.zh: 死事者哭之而育其孤，或以子婚其女。

translations.literal: for those who died in service he wept and raised their orphans, or married his sons to their daughters.
translations.idiomatic: for those who died in service he wept and raised their orphans, or married his sons to their daughters.

sentences.zh: 凡有頒犒，均給軍吏，秋毫不私。

translations.literal: Whenever rewards were distributed, he shared them equally among officers and soldiers, keeping not a fraction for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rewards were distributed, he shared them equally among officers and men—not a fraction for himself.

sentences.zh: 善以少擊衆。

translations.literal: He was skilled at defeating large forces with small numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at defeating large forces with small numbers.

sentences.zh: 欲有所舉，盡召諸統制與謀，謀定而後戰，故有勝無敗。

translations.literal: When he planned an operation, he summoned all the unit commanders to counsel together; only after the plan was settled did he fight—hence victory and never defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Before any operation he summoned all his unit commanders to counsel together. Only when the plan was settled did he fight—hence victory after victory, never defeat.

sentences.zh: 猝遇敵不動，故敵為之語曰：「撼山易，撼岳家軍難。

translations.literal: When suddenly encountering the enemy he did not flinch; therefore the enemy had a saying: "It is easy to shake a mountain; it is hard to shake Yue's army.
translations.idiomatic: When suddenly encountering the enemy he never flinched. The enemy had a saying: "It is easy to shake a mountain; it is hard to shake the Yue family army."

sentences.zh: 」張俊嘗問用兵之術，曰：「仁、智、信、勇、嚴，闕一不可。

translations.literal: " Zhang Jun once asked about the art of war; Fei said, "Benevolence, wisdom, trustworthiness, courage, and strictness—leave out one and it will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun once asked about the art of war. Yue Fei said: "Benevolence, wisdom, trustworthiness, courage, and strictness—leave out one and it will not do."

sentences.zh: 」調軍食，必蹙額曰：「東南民力，耗敝極矣。

translations.literal: " When requisitioning army provisions, he always furrowed his brow and said, "The strength of the people in the southeast is exhausted to the limit.
