translations.idiomatic: When requisitioning army provisions he always furrowed his brow: "The people of the southeast are exhausted to the breaking point."

sentences.zh: 」荊湖平，募民營田，又為屯田，歲省漕運之半。

translations.literal: " After the Jing and Hu regions were pacified, he recruited civilians for garrison farming and also established military colonies, saving half the grain transport each year.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jing and Hu regions were pacified, he recruited civilians for garrison farming and established military colonies, cutting grain transport costs in half each year.

sentences.zh: 帝手書曹操、諸葛亮、羊祜三事賜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote out by hand three accounts—of Cao Cao, Zhuge Liang, and Yang Hu—and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote out by hand accounts of Cao Cao, Zhuge Liang, and Yang Hu and bestowed them on him.

sentences.zh: 飛跋其後，獨指操為姦賊而鄙之，尤檜所惡也。

translations.literal: Fei wrote a colophon afterward, singling out Cao Cao alone as a treacherous villain and despising him—this Qin Hui especially hated.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei wrote a colophon afterward, singling out Cao Cao alone as a treacherous villain and despising him—this Qin Hui especially hated.

sentences.zh: 張所死，飛感舊恩，鞠其子宗本，奏以官。

translations.literal: When Zhang Suo died, Fei, moved by old kindness, raised his son Zongben and memorialized to grant him office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Suo died, Yue Fei, moved by old kindness, raised his son Zongben and memorialized to grant him office.

sentences.zh: 李寶自楚來歸，韓世忠留之，寶痛哭願歸飛，世忠以書來諗，飛復曰：「均為國家，何分彼此？

translations.literal: Li Bao came over from Chu; Han Shizhong kept him; Bao wept and begged to return to Fei; Shizhong wrote to consult Fei, and Fei replied, "We all serve the state—why distinguish between us?
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao came over from Chu. Han Shizhong kept him. Li Bao wept and begged to serve Yue Fei. Han Shizhong wrote to consult Yue Fei, who replied: "We all serve the state—why distinguish between us?"

sentences.zh: 」世忠嘆服。

translations.literal: " Shizhong sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 襄陽之役，詔光世為援，六郡既復，光世始至，飛奏先賞光世軍。

translations.literal: In the Xiangyang campaign, Liu Guangshi was ordered as reinforcement; after the six prefectures were recovered, Guangshi only then arrived; Fei memorialized to reward Guangshi's army first.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiangyang campaign Liu Guangshi was ordered as reinforcement. After the six prefectures were recovered Guangshi only then arrived. Yue Fei memorialized to reward Liu Guangshi's army first.

sentences.zh: 好賢禮士，覽經史，雅歌投壺，恂恂如書生。

translations.literal: He loved worthies and honored scholars, read the classics and histories, sang refined songs and played pitch-pot, and was deferential as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He loved worthies and honored scholars, read the classics and histories, sang refined songs and played pitch-pot—deferential as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 每辭官，必曰：「將士効力，飛何功之有？

translations.literal: Whenever he declined honors, he always said, "The officers and soldiers gave their strength—what merit has Fei?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he declined honors he always said: "The officers and soldiers gave their strength—what merit have I?"

sentences.zh: 」然忠憤激烈，議論持正，不挫於人，卒以此得禍。

translations.literal: " Yet his loyal indignation was fierce; his opinions were upright and he would not yield to others—in the end he came to harm because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his loyal indignation was fierce, his opinions upright, and he would not yield to others—in the end this brought him to ruin.

sentences.zh: 檜死，議復飛官。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui died, there was discussion of restoring Fei's offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui died, there was discussion of restoring Yue Fei's offices.

sentences.zh: 万俟禼謂金方願和，一旦錄故將，疑天下心，不可。

translations.literal: Wan Qixie said the Jin just then wished for peace; to suddenly rehabilitate a former general would arouse suspicion in the hearts of the realm—it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Qixie argued that the Jin wished for peace; to suddenly rehabilitate a former general would arouse suspicion throughout the realm—it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 及紹興末，金益猖獗，太學生程宏圖上書訟飛冤，詔飛家自便。

translations.literal: By the end of the Shaoxing era the Jin grew ever more aggressive; Imperial University student Cheng Hongtu submitted a memorial pleading Fei's injustice, and an edict allowed Fei's family to move freely.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Shaoxing era the Jin grew ever bolder. Imperial University student Cheng Hongtu submitted a memorial pleading Yue Fei's injustice, and an edict allowed the Yue family to move freely.

sentences.zh: 初，檜惡岳州同飛姓，改為純州，至是仍舊。

translations.literal: Earlier Qin Hui had hated that Yue Prefecture shared Fei's surname and changed it to Chun Prefecture; now it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui had hated that Yue Prefecture shared the Yue surname and changed it to Chun Prefecture. Now it was restored.

sentences.zh: 中丞汪澈宣撫荊、襄，故部曲合辭訟之，哭聲雷震。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Che was sent to pacify Jing and Xiang; Fei's former troops together pleaded his injustice, their wailing like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Che was sent to pacify Jing and Xiang. Yue Fei's former troops together pleaded his injustice—their wailing like thunder.

sentences.zh: 孝宗詔復飛官，以禮改葬，賜錢百萬，求其後悉官之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong ordered Fei's offices restored, a proper reburial, a gift of a million cash, and that all his descendants be found and given office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong ordered Yue Fei's offices restored, a proper reburial, a gift of a million cash, and that all his descendants be found and given office.

sentences.zh: 建廟於鄂，號忠烈。

translations.literal: A temple was built at E, titled Loyal and Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was built at Ezhou, titled Loyal and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 淳熙六年，謚武穆。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chunxi he was given the posthumous title Martial and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chunxi he was given the posthumous title Martial and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年，追封鄂王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiading he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of E.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiading he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of E.

sentences.zh: 五子：雲、雷、霖、震、霆。

translations.literal: Five sons: Yun, Lei, Lin, Zhen, and Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons: Yun, Lei, Lin, Zhen, and Ting.

sentences.zh: 子 雲

translations.literal: Son: Yun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yun

sentences.zh: 雲，飛養子。

translations.literal: Yun was Fei's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was Yue Fei's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 年十二，從張憲戰，多得其力，軍中呼曰「贏官人」。

translations.literal: At twelve he followed Zhang Xian into battle and contributed greatly; the army called him "Lord Winner."
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he followed Zhang Xian into battle and contributed greatly. The army called him "Lord Winner."

sentences.zh: 飛征伐，未嘗不與，數立奇功，飛輒隱之。

translations.literal: In Fei's campaigns he was never absent; he repeatedly achieved extraordinary merit, but Fei always concealed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yue Fei's campaigns he was never absent. He repeatedly achieved extraordinary merit, but Yue Fei always concealed it.

sentences.zh: 每戰，以手握兩鐵椎，重八十斤，先諸軍登城。

translations.literal: In every battle he gripped two iron maces weighing eighty jin and was first among the army to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he gripped two iron maces weighing eighty jin and was first among the army to scale the walls.

sentences.zh: 攻下隨州，又攻破鄧州，襄漢平，功在第一，飛不言。

translations.literal: He captured Suizhou and then broke Dengzhou; when Xiang and Han were pacified his merit ranked first, but Fei said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Suizhou and then took Dengzhou. When Xiang and Han were pacified his merit ranked first—but Yue Fei said nothing.

sentences.zh: 逾年，銓曹辯之，始遷武翼郎、楊么平，功亦第一，又不上。

translations.literal: More than a year later the personnel office investigated and he was first promoted to Martial Wing Gentleman; when Yang Yao was pacified his merit again ranked first, and again he did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the personnel office investigated and he was promoted to Martial Wing Gentleman. When Yang Yao was pacified his merit again ranked first—and again he did not report it.

sentences.zh: 張浚廉得其實，曰：「岳侯避寵榮，廉則廉矣，未得為公也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun investigated and learned the truth; he said, "Lord Yue avoids honors and glory—honorable he is, but this is not fair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun investigated and learned the truth. He said: "Lord Yue avoids honors and glory—honorable, yes, but this is not fair."

sentences.zh: 」奏乞推異數，飛力辭不受。

translations.literal: " He memorialized asking to grant extraordinary honors; Fei forcefully declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to grant extraordinary honors. Yue Fei forcefully declined.

sentences.zh: 嘗以特旨遷三資，飛辭曰：「士卒冒矢石立奇功，始沾一級，男雲遽躐崇資，何以服衆？

translations.literal: Once by special edict he was promoted three ranks; Fei declined, saying, "Soldiers who face arrows and stones to achieve extraordinary merit barely gain one rank—how can my son Yun suddenly leap to high honors? How will this satisfy the troops?
translations.idiomatic: Once by special edict he was promoted three ranks. Yue Fei declined: "Soldiers who face arrows and stones barely gain one rank—how can my son Yun suddenly leap to high honors? How will this satisfy the troops?"

sentences.zh: 」累表不受。

translations.literal: " He repeatedly memorialized and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized and refused.

sentences.zh: 穎昌大戰，無慮十數，出入行陣，體被百餘創，甲裳為赤。

translations.literal: In the great battles at Yingchang there were no fewer than a dozen; he went in and out of the battle lines and his body bore more than a hundred wounds—his armor and garments were dyed red.
translations.idiomatic: In the great battles at Yingchang there were no fewer than a dozen. He went in and out of the battle lines and his body bore more than a hundred wounds—his armor and garments were dyed red.

sentences.zh: 以功遷忠州防禦使，飛又辭；

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Defender of Zhong Prefecture; Fei again declined;
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Defender of Zhong Prefecture. Yue Fei again declined.

sentences.zh: 命帶御器械，飛又力辭之。

translations.literal: he was ordered to carry the imperial arms; Fei again forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to carry the imperial arms. Yue Fei again forcefully declined.

sentences.zh: 終左武大夫、提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: In the end he held the rank of Left Martial Grand Master and was Commissioner of the Liquan View.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he held the rank of Left Martial Grand Master and was Commissioner of the Liquan View.

sentences.zh: 死年二十三。

translations.literal: He died at twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 孝宗初，與飛同復元官，以禮祔葬，贈安遠軍承宣使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozong's reign his original offices were restored along with Fei's; he was buried by rite beside Fei and posthumously made Military Commissioner of Anyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaozong's reign his original offices were restored along with Yue Fei's. He was buried by rite beside Yue Fei and posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Anyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 雷，忠訓郎、閣門祗候，贈武略郎。

translations.literal: Lei was Loyal Training Gentleman and Palace Gate Attendant; posthumously made Martial Strategy Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Lei was Loyal Training Gentleman and Palace Gate Attendant; posthumously made Martial Strategy Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 霖，朝散大夫、敷文閣待制，贈太中大夫。

translations.literal: Lin was Gentleman for Dispersing Affairs and Attendant Drafting Master at the Fuwen Pavilion; posthumously made Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was Gentleman for Dispersing Affairs and Attendant Drafting Master at the Fuwen Pavilion; posthumously made Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 初，飛下獄，檜令親黨王會搜其家，得御札數篋，束之左藏南庫，霖請於孝宗，還之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fei was imprisoned, Qin Hui ordered his kinsman Wang Hui to search his home; several cases of imperial letters were found and stored in the Left Treasury's south vault; Lin petitioned Xiaozong and they were returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Fei was imprisoned Qin Hui ordered his kinsman Wang Hui to search his home. Several cases of imperial letters were found and stored in the Left Treasury's south vault. Lin petitioned Xiaozong and they were returned.

sentences.zh: 霖子珂，以淮西十五御札辯驗彙次，凡出師應援之先後皆可考。

translations.literal: Lin's son Ke used fifteen imperial letters from the Huai West affair to verify and compile them in order; the sequence of all deployments and reinforcements could be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's son Ke used fifteen imperial letters from the Huai West affair to verify and compile them in order—the sequence of every deployment and reinforcement could be checked.

sentences.zh: 嘉定間，為《籲天辯誣集》五卷、《天定錄》二捲上之。

translations.literal: During the Jiading era he compiled the five-scroll Appeal to Heaven Refuting False Charges and the two-scroll Record of Heaven's Verdict and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiading era he compiled the five-scroll Appeal to Heaven Refuting False Charges and the two-scroll Record of Heaven's Verdict and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 震，朝奉大夫、提舉江南東路茶鹽公事。

translations.literal: Zhen was Gentleman for Court Attendance and Commissioner for Tea and Salt Affairs of Jiangnan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was Gentleman for Court Attendance and Commissioner for Tea and Salt Affairs of Jiangnan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 霆，修武郎、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Ting was Gentleman of Cultivated Martiality and Palace Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ting held the ranks of Gentleman of Cultivated Martiality and Palace Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 論曰：西漢而下，若韓、彭、絳、灌之為將，代不乏人，求其文武全器、仁智幷施如宋岳飛者，一代豈多見哉。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: From the Western Han down, as generals like Han, Peng, Zhou Bo, and Guan Ying, each age has not lacked such men; but to seek one who combined civil and martial excellence in full measure, who applied both benevolence and wisdom as did Yue Fei of Song—how often in a generation is such a one seen?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Since the Western Han, each age has produced commanders in the mold of Han Xin, Peng Yue, Zhou Bo, and Guan Ying—yet to find one who united civil and martial gifts and wielded both benevolence and wisdom as Yue Fei of Song did is a rarity indeed in any generation.

sentences.zh: 史稱關雲長通《春秋左氏》學，然未嘗見其文章。

translations.literal: History says Guan Yunchang mastered the learning of the 《Zuo Commentary》, yet his writings have never been seen.
translations.idiomatic: History tells us that Guan Yu mastered the 《Zuo Commentary》, yet none of his writings survive.

sentences.zh: 飛北伐，軍至汴梁之朱仙鎮，有詔班師，飛自為表答詔，忠義之言，流出肺腑，真有諸葛孔明之風，而卒死於秦檜之手。

translations.literal: When Fei marched north and his army reached Zhuxian Town of Bianliang, an edict ordered withdrawal; Fei himself drafted the memorial in reply to the edict, words of loyalty and righteousness pouring from his inmost heart, truly in the manner of Zhuge Kongming—yet in the end he died at the hands of Qin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: On his northern campaign Yue Fei reached Zhuxian Town outside Bianliang when an edict recalled the army. He drafted the reply himself—words of loyalty and righteousness that seemed to pour straight from the heart, worthy of Zhuge Liang himself—yet he died at Qin Hui's hands in the end.

sentences.zh: 蓋飛與檜勢不兩立，使飛得志，則金讎可復，宋恥可雪；

translations.literal: For Fei and Hui could not both stand; had Fei achieved his aim, the Jin enemy could have been avenged and Song's shame wiped away;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei and Qin Hui could not coexist: had Yue Fei had his way, the Jin could have been avenged and Song's humiliation erased;

sentences.zh: 檜得志，則飛有死而已。

translations.literal: had Hui achieved his aim, Fei had only death.
translations.idiomatic: once Qin Hui prevailed, Yue Fei could only die.

sentences.zh: 昔劉宋殺檀道濟，道濟下獄，嗔目曰：「自壞汝萬里長城！

translations.literal: In former times the Liu-Song killed Tan Daoji; when Daoji was thrown into prison he glared and said, "You are destroying your own ten-thousand-li Great Wall!"
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Liu-Song dynasty executed Tan Daoji. As he was thrown into prison he glared and cried, "You are tearing down your own Great Wall!"

sentences.zh: 」高宗忍自棄其中原，故忍殺飛，嗚呼寃哉！

translations.literal: " Gaozong could bear to abandon the Central Plains himself, and so could bear to kill Fei—alas, what injustice!
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozong could bring himself to abandon the Central Plains, and so could bring himself to kill Yue Fei—what an outrage!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼寃哉！

translations.literal: Alas, what injustice!
translations.idiomatic: What an outrage!
